title: U.S. Senator Katie Britt’s Advocacy Helps Secure $8.1 Million Federal Investment in County Road 13 in Daphne
text:
Funding will add roundabouts, lighting, sidewalks and school-zone crosswalks along one of Baldwin County’s highest-crash corridors

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Sen. Katie Britt (R-Ala.) today celebrated the City of Daphne being awarded $8,100,530 from the U.S. Department of Transportation’s Safe Streets and Roads for All (SS4A) grant program to make critical safety improvements along County Road 13 in Baldwin County. Senator Britt wrote a letter in support of the city’s application.

“Every family in Daphne deserves to get to work, school, and home safely, and this investment will help make that a reality on one of Baldwin County’s busiest roads,” said Senator Britt. “I was proud to support the City of Daphne’s application and advocate for this project, and I’m grateful to Secretary Duffy for recognizing how important this corridor is to the community. With three schools along this stretch and more than 130 crashes in just five years, these roundabouts, lights, sidewalks, and crosswalks will save lives. I’ll keep fighting to make sure Alabama communities have the resources they need to keep our roads safe.”

The project will improve 2.5 miles of County Road 13 from County Road 64/Daphne Road to Champions Way/Lawson Road. Planned upgrades include converting the intersections at Pleasant Road and Champions Way to roundabouts, adding lighting along the corridor, installing 8-foot sidewalks, and adding crosswalks at school zones and the new roundabouts.

The corridor, which carries about 9,600 vehicles each day, is identified on the city’s Action Plan high-injury network. Between 2019 and 2023, it saw 132 crashes, including three suspected serious injury crashes. 27% of those crashes occurred in dark, dawn, or dusk conditions.

“We extend our sincere appreciation to Senator Katie Britt for her continued support and collaboration with Secretary Duffy in securing an $8 million grant dedicated to improving safety for all travelers along the CR 13 corridor. This significant investment will help enhance transportation safety, improve quality of life, and benefit the residents of Daphne and communities throughout Baldwin County.

“We are grateful for Senator Britt’s continued commitment to Daphne, the Eastern Shore, and Baldwin County. Her leadership and continued success in securing critical infrastructure funding is making a meaningful difference in our communities and strengthening the future of Alabama.

“Thank you, Senator Britt, for your continued partnership and dedication to the people of Baldwin County and the State of Alabama,” said Daphne Mayor Robin LeJeune.

The improvements rely on Federal Highway Administration Proven Safety Countermeasures—roundabouts, lighting, sidewalks and high-visibility crosswalks—to reduce the risk of rear-end, angle, head-on and pedestrian crashes. The project is expected to lower speeds, reduce conflict points, and create safer crossings near three schools. The new roundabouts are estimated to reduce all crashes at those intersections by 21.7%, and corridor lighting is expected to cut crashes along the route by 32%.

This more than $8 million in funding is part of more than $37 million in grants awarded to projects across the state of Alabama. Senator Britt has previously written letters of support for several of these road safety projects.

title: Budd Leads Congressional Colleagues in Advocating for New Autonomous Warfare Command to Be Headquartered in North Carolina
text:
Washington, D.C. — U.S. Senator Ted Budd (R-N.C.) today led several North Carolina Congressional colleagues in sending a bipartisan letter to Secretary of War Pete Hegseth urging him to select the State of North Carolina to serve as the headquarters for the Autonomous Warfare Command (AUTOWARCOM), a new, functional combatant command that will lead the joint force in unmanned autonomous warfare.

In the letter, the Members wrote:

“North Carolina hosts an expansive defense industrial base, innovative research institutes and universities, strategic terrain, and well-equipped military installations; home to some of our nation’s top warfighters. Our delegation has consistently emphasized North Carolina’s unique ability to contribute to missions of national importance, and our state continues to deliver to this end. North Carolina’s military installations, including Fort Bragg and Camp Lejeune, have already emerged as national leaders in the integration of emerging technologies and advanced weapons systems into the force.”

Joining Senator Budd in sending this letter are Representatives Don Davis (D-N.C.-01), Virginia Foxx (R-N.C.-05), Pat Harrigan (R-N.C.-10), Mark Harris (R-N.C.-08), Richard Hudson (R-N.C.-09), Brad Knott (R-N.C.-13), Addison McDowell (R-N.C.-06), Tim Moore (R-N.C.-14), Greg Murphy (R-N.C.-03), and Deborah Ross (D-N.C.-02).

Read the full text of the letter HERE and below:

Dear Secretary Hegseth,

We write in support of the Department of War’s Autonomous Warfare Command (AUTOWARCOM) proposal, and to recommend that the combatant command be headquartered in North Carolina. North Carolina hosts an expansive defense industrial base, innovative research institutes and universities, strategic terrain, and well-equipped military installations; home to some of our nation’s top warfighters. Our delegation has consistently emphasized North Carolina’s unique ability to contribute to missions of national importance, and our state continues to deliver to this end.

North Carolina’s military installations, including Fort Bragg and Camp Lejeune, have already emerged as national leaders in the integration of emerging technologies and advanced weapons systems into the force. Fort Bragg is home to expeditionary forces, including the XVIII Airborne Corps, which executes the Scarlet Dragon and the Sandhills Project exercises alongside industry to advance autonomous, attritable mass capabilities, and the new Joint Innovation Outpost. At Camp Lejeune, Marines conducted the Marine Corps’ first live-fire test of lethal drone munitions in July 2025 and now train units on first-person-view attack drones.

In addition to the cutting-edge training conducted by the XVIII Airborne Corps and the Marines at Camp Lejeune, Seymour Johnson Air Force Base and Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point also contribute to the state’s robust military presence, providing North Carolina with a diverse community of combat aviators. This, coupled with the U.S. Army Special Operations Command at Fort Bragg, is demonstrative of the state’s elite community of tacticians, trained to execute at the highest levels.

Further, North Carolina has a robust industry presence and startup ecosystem already developing autonomous systems for the military and commercial sectors alike. Companies across the state are working to design, develop, manufacture, and test autonomous systems—often partnering with North Carolina’s top-flight universities and research institutions. The state’s diverse and strategic terrain, including the Blue Ridge Mountains, the Sandhills region, and the coastal Atlantic region, offer unique testing locations equipped to simulate a variety of fighting conditions.

North Carolina has the warfighters, the industry, and the research base to make AUTOWARCOM successful from day one. Thank you for your attention to this important matter and we look forward to your response.

Sincerely,

/X/

title: PHOTO: Capito Attends Ribbon Cutting for Kanawha County Ambulance Authority’s South Charleston Substation
text:
SOUTH CHARLESTON, W.Va. – Today, U.S. Senator Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.) traveled to South Charleston, W.Va. to attend the ribbon cutting of Kanawha County Emergency Ambulance Authority’s South Charleston substation, which she helped secure a Fiscal Year 2023 (FY23) $750,000 Congressionally Directed Spending (CDS) award for. While there, Senator Capito delivered remarks and celebrated alongside local leaders and city officials.

“It was great to participate in today's ribbon cutting for Kanawha County Ambulance Authority’s new South Charleston substation,” Senator Capito said. “I was proud to have helped secure federal funding for this project to address the needs of our first responders and improve EMS response times. This station represents an investment in the health and well-being of our communities and the dedicated first responders who work every day to keep them safe. I look forward to the positive impact it will have on our communities for years to come.”

“We’re grateful to Senator Capito for helping secure the funding for these substations and for her continued support of first responders across West Virginia. This investment will benefit our crews and the communities they serve for years to come. We appreciate having a partner in Washington who listens to first responders and works to make sure they have the resources to do their jobs,” KCEAA Executive Director Lance Wheeler said.

BACKGROUND:

Senator Capito has been a longtime supporter of Kanawha County Emergency Ambulance Authority and has secured numerous funding awards to support community safety and disaster response. In addition to the South Charleston substation, Senator Capito helped secure funding for new stations in Dunbar, St. Albans, and Marmet. Most recently, she helped secured a $2.1 million Congressionally Directed Spending Award (CDS) award for the purchase of six new emergency vehicles, and a $4 million Safe Streets Grant from the U.S. Department of Transportation for KCEAA to develop a Supplemental Action Plan and conduct demonstration activities focused on improving post-crash care, responder coordination, and roadway safety.

title: Cortez Masto Leads Democratic Colleagues in Requesting Answers from X On Apparent Preferential Treatment of Polymarket
text:
Las Vegas, Nev. – U.S. Senator Catherine Cortez Masto (D-Nev.) led Senators Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.), Jacky Rosen (D-Nev.), and Adam Schiff (D-Calif.) in a letter to X (formerly Twitter) Chief Compliance Officer C. Rob DeCampos requesting answers on the seemingly preferential treatment Polymarket is receiving from X. The Senators raise concern that, due to Donald Trump Jr.’s role as an adviser and investor for Polymarket, any preferential treatment could help the President and his family enrich themselves.

The Senators explained: “Typically, X allows users to report an ad for a myriad of reasons; however, when attempting to report Polymarket’s ads through the standard X interface, users are denied the option to do so (Figure A). This is not the case with other types of advertisements, including Kalshi, another prediction markets platform offering sports gaming that is illegal in states across the U.S., including in Nevada (Figure B).”

“This seemingly preferential treatment calls into question whether X is attempting to provide an undue competitive advantage to Polymarket and – by extension – the President and his family,” the Senators continue. “It would not be the first time Donald Trump Jr. has attempted to use his position to enrich himself. Earlier this year, he reportedly pressured a room of Republican state attorneys general to stop trying to regulate prediction markets, which he is heavily invested in.”

Read the full letter here.

Senators Cortez Masto has repeatedly called for more stringent oversight of prediction markets. The Senator has previously called on the CFTC to prohibit prediction markets incentivizing physical injury, death, or war; has raised the alarm about offshore prediction markets allowing people to bet on wildfires; and pushed the CFTC to do more to combat insider trading in prediction markets. Cortez Masto has also urged CFTC Chair Michael Selig to abstain from intervening in pending litigation involving prediction markets. The Senator is a co-sponsor of the Prediction Markets Are Gambling Act, which would prohibit CFTC-registered entities – like Polymarket and Kalshi – from listing any prediction contracts that resemble a sports bet or casino-style game.

title: Cramer Announces UND Space Operations Summit Guest
text:
BISMARCK, N.D. – With the University of North Dakota’s (UND) Space Operations Summit less than a week away from liftoff, U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) announced Brad Clevenger will join him at the event on Nov. 4 in Grand Forks. Clevenger, the President of Rocket Lab USA, and Cramer will discover the latest in space technology, applications, and services at the event, which also features discussions, technical sessions, and networking opportunities on a wide variety of trailblazing ideas.

Clevenger, who leads Rocket Lab’s Space Systems segment, provides strategic leadership across the company’s satellite and satellite component business units. His extensive experience and leadership in the space industry make him an ideal guest to join Cramer for a discussion on the rapidly evolving space sector, its emerging technologies, the industry’s growth trajectory, and advancements in space and launch capabilities.

Rocket Lab recently announced plans to acquire Iridium Communications, a leading global provider of voice, data, and Positioning, Navigation, and Timing (PNT) satellite services. North Dakota is home to Space Development Agency’s (SDA) 25,000 square-foot Satellite Test and Checkout Center at Grand Forks Air Force Base, where Iridium employs dozens of highly skilled workers who help conduct operations for SDA’s low-earth-orbit missions.

“Companies like Rocket Lab are playing an important role in strengthening our national security in space,” said Cramer. “And with more than two decades of experience in satellite missions and space technology, Brad Clevenger has a great perspective on where this industry is headed and the incredible advancements happening across the sector. I’m really honored he’s accepted my invitation to join me in Grand Forks for this year’s Space Operations Summit, and I’m looking forward to our conversation.”

“I’m grateful to Senator Cramer for inviting me to be his guest at the University of North Dakota’s Space Operations Summit,” said Brad Clevenger, President of Rocket Lab USA. “Now more than ever, it’s critical for industry innovators like Rocket Lab to be part of these key conversations between academia, U.S. government, and industry on how best we can collaborate to ensure American space superiority. Senator Cramer’s leadership on these issues in the United States Senate is invaluable and I look forward to discussing Rocket Lab’s perspective more during our fireside chat.”

Before joining Rocket Lab, Clevenger held several executive leadership roles at SolAero Technologies and EMCORE Corporation. Clevenger has contributed to more than 250 satellite missions and the deployment of over 1,100 satellites over his two decades in the industry. Under his leadership, the business grew into a global leader in satellite solar power technology.

title: Cramer Requests HHS, CMS Implement Phased Approach, Collaboration With Medicaid Expansion, Rural Health Funding
text:
BISMARCK, N.D. – U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) sent a letter today to U.S. Health and Human Services (HHS) Secretary Robert Kennedy, Jr. and Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Dr. Mehmet Oz requesting a reasonable glidepath and collaborative partnership regarding North Dakota’s Medicaid expansion program and implementation of the Rural Health Transformation Program (RHTP). CMS is currently reviewing the state’s Medicaid expansion reimbursement program per a proposed rule relating to state directed payments. CMS is also partnering with North Dakota to administer the RHTP to support rural hospitals and transform healthcare delivery.

Cramer’s letter highlighted the state’s unique healthcare delivery challenges, including a large rural population and long travel distances, and the importance of Medicaid reimbursement in sustaining a reliable delivery system. Abrupt changes to existing payment arrangements could create disruption for providers, patients and communities. Cramer requested a phased approach that will provide stability while creating opportunities for RHTP investments to expand innovation and enhance access, especially in the state’s more rural areas.

“I have heard from many stakeholders across the state with concerns about proposed changes to Medicaid expansion reimbursement and the impact of such changes on healthcare delivery,” said Cramer. “To help address these concerns, I requested Secretary Kennedy and Administrator Oz work with North Dakota on a phased approach to implementing any changes and partner on harnessing the RHTP to transform healthcare in our state. This glidepath approach paired with the RHTP investment would support the pioneering work already underway in our state and create generational changes to our rural healthcare ecosystem.”

Cramer stated that without a phased approach, providers could face a fiscal cliff, and a reasonable glidepath would provide the state and affected providers sufficient time to adjust to new requirements and mitigate any disruptions to the state’s healthcare delivery system. Cramer requested the agency work closely with North Dakota to establish an appropriate glidepath and phased implementation schedule for any identified changes.

The RHTP, a $50 billion investment created through the Working Families Tax Cut Act, reflects Congress’ commitment to protecting taxpayers and ensuring the long-term sustainability of federal healthcare programs broadly. The legislation also included a tiered pathway to reduce certain approved state directed payments beginning Jan. 1, 2028, with rates reducing annually until the target is reached.

title: FCC Chairman Carr Visits North Dakota, Participates in UAS and Local Broadcasters Roundtables
text:
***Click herefor media resources.***

FARGO, N.D. – U.S. Senator Kevin Cramer (R-ND) welcomed Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chairman Brendan Carr to North Dakota for a series of visits and roundtable discussions focused on the state’s role in deploying next-generation unmanned aircraft systems (UAS) and his efforts to ensure community newsrooms can compete in the Digital Age. Cramer said the visit “highlighted North Dakota’s role in advancing UAS technology and protecting the ability of local broadcasters to provide the local news, entertainment, and emergency coverage their listeners rely on.”

“As the chief regulator of the broadcast industry, the FCC is responsible for ensuring its regulations serve the public interest and foster local journalism, particularly at a time more Americans are turning to social media and streaming services for the information they consume daily,” said Cramer. “At the same time, the agency is helping to shape the future of our airspace and advance the next generation of unmanned aircraft technology. I’m grateful Chairman Carr took the time to visit North Dakota, see the innovation happening here, and hear directly from the people and industries driving it forward.”

“I want to thank Senator Cramer for inviting me back to North Dakota,” said Chairman Carr. “He is a great advocate for the state and its range of innovative industries. From promoting American drone dominance to modernizing broadcast regulations, Senator Cramer has made sure that the FCC delivers for North Dakota. I look forward to acting on the many good ideas we heard today.”

Cramer and Carr began their visit in Emerado where they toured General Atomics and Northrop Grumman facilities operating out of Grand Sky, the first public-private UAS park in the United States. Afterwards, they participated in a roundtable discussion focused on the growing role of unmanned aircraft technology, its applications, and the opportunities it presents for North Dakota’s aerospace and defense industries.

They then traveled to Fargo for a roundtable with local broadcasters to discuss the importance of television and radio stations in keeping North Dakotans informed and connected.

Cramer and Carr also toured Badland Batteries, a battery cell manufacturing facility in Fargo, which combines automated and manned equipment to produce lithium-ion pouch cells for defense, aerospace, and autonomous systems.

title: Duckworth Demands Answers on Trump’s Dangerously Low Halloween Flyover at the White House
text:
[WASHINGTON, D.C.] – U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL)—Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Commerce Subcommittee on Aviation—today demanded answers from the Trump Administration on Donald Trump’s reckless, dangerously low White House flyover during last week’s Halloween festivities, which frightened local residents, jeopardized safety and likely cost taxpayers hundreds of thousands of dollars for no good reason. In her letter to Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth, Federal Aviation Administrator Bryan Bedford and Director of the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) Russell Vought, Duckworth lambasted the group for allowing Trump to pull this irresponsible, expensive vanity stunt in one of the most congested and restricted airspaces in the country—all while the American people struggle to pay higher prices for gas, groceries and health care as a direct result of the President’s disastrous policies.

“The stunt startled residents, prompted 911 calls, forced a ground stop at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), contributed to more than 200 flight delays and burned taxpayer dollars so President Trump could parade his toy before children trick-or-treating on the South Lawn. For the children on the lawn, perhaps a treat; for everyone else in the National Capital Region (NCR) and across the country, a trick—dangerous, expensive and profoundly unserious,” wrote Duckworth.

“The recent flyover was presumably flown with DoD operational and training funds—meaning American taxpayers footed the bill. Families are struggling with the cost of gas and groceries, driven up by President Trump’s war of choice against Iran and his chaotic tariffs, and the President has dismissed their concerns as a ‘hoax.’ A serious President would be bringing costs down. This one is busy showing off his toys, putting on full display how wildly out of touch he is with the needs of the American people,” continued Duckworth.

The Senator also slammed the Administration officials for working quickly to allow this dangerous, ego-driven stunt while they show no urgency to lower costs or make our skies safer. Namely, Duckworth cited the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) and Department of Defense’s (DoD) ongoing failure to address the urgent safety recommendations made by the National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) to ensure that a tragedy like the DCA midair collision never happens again.

“When former President Obama likened the President’s gilded White House renovations to a Cheesecake Factory, official White House accounts and a Cabinet Secretary rushed to defend the décor within 48 hours. This Administration moves with urgency when the President’s taste is questioned but with none when the American people struggle with the soaring cost of living or the NTSB warns of a ‘continued and unacceptable risk to public safety,’” Duckworth continued.

To ensure the American people receive an explanation for why their taxpayer money was burned on this reckless stunt, Duckworth is demanding that Hegseth, Bedford and Vought provide a detailed accounting of how the flyover was approved, why so little notice was given, what training objective—if any—it served and how much it cost taxpayers, among other questions.

Full text of the letter can be found below and on Senator Duckworth’s website:

Dear Administrator Bedford, Secretary Hegseth and Director Vought:

I write to demand a full accounting of the two low-altitude flyovers of downtown Washington, D.C., on October 29, 2026, by the luxury Boeing 747 that the Emir of Qatar gifted to Donald Trump, and which the White House insists on calling “Air Force One” even when President Donald Trump is standing on the ground watching it. The stunt startled residents, prompted 911 calls, forced a ground stop at Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport (DCA), contributed to more than 200 flight delays and burned taxpayer dollars so President Trump could parade his toy before children trick-or-treating on the South Lawn. For the children on the lawn, perhaps a treat; for everyone else in the National Capital Region (NCR) and across the country, a trick—dangerous, expensive and profoundly unserious.

Flight-tracking data show the aircraft made two passes over the White House between roughly 400 and 1,000 feet and, according to videos, the aircraft flew near or below the top of the Washington Monument (555 feet). In the most restricted airspace in the country, this dangerous stunt was below the minimum safe altitude required by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) of every civil aircraft over a congested area under 14 CFR § 91.119. The D.C. Council reported that downtown D.C., the Pentagon and DCA received just 15 minutes’ notice; AlertDC did not warn residents until 5:24 p.m.; airlines reportedly had less than an hour; and, Administrator Bedford, the FAA has declined to say when it first learned of the flyover. Residents who lived through September 11, 2001, when a hijacked airliner struck the Pentagon, dialed 911 fearing an attack. The White House insisted the flyover “brought joy and excitement.” Tell that to the people who called 911.

It is a disgraceful dereliction of duty that dishonors the memories of the passengers, crew and servicemembers that were killed on January 29, 2025, for the FAA and the U.S. Department of Defense (DoD) to spend finite time making the airspace around DCA less safe for an evening when neither agency has closed out the National Transportation Safety Board’s (NTSB) recommendations following the January 29, 2025, midair collision that claimed 67 lives. The FAA has closed only three of the 35 recommendations the NTSB directed to it; 11 directed to DoD remain open; the NTSB has deemed 11 FAA responses “unacceptable”; and more than 600 days later there is still no FAA–DoD memorandum of understanding for the NCR airspace. Yet the same agencies found the capacity to coordinate two low passes of a 747 over the White House and impose a ground stop at DCA to do it.

This administration’s track record on flyover coordination in NCR airspace is alarming. On March 28, 2025, only 58 days after the DCA midair collision, a timing miscommunication between Potomac Consolidated TRACON and the DCA tower caused a four-ship formation of U.S. Air Force T-38 Talon trainer jets inbound for a ceremonial flyover at Arlington National Cemetery and departing Delta Air Lines Flight 2983, carrying 131 passengers, to cross paths dangerously closely. Nineteen months later, the same two agencies scrambled a 747 over the White House on fifteen minutes’ notice. When will the Trump administration learn?

The recent flyover was presumably flown with DoD operational and training funds—meaning American taxpayers footed the bill. Families are struggling with the cost of gas and groceries, driven up by President Trump’s war of choice against Iran and his chaotic tariffs, and the President has dismissed their concerns as a “hoax.” A serious President would be bringing costs down. This one is busy showing off his toys, putting on full display how wildly out of touch he is with the needs of the American people.

Last Thursday’s flyover is only the latest in a pattern. Last month, the National Park Service abruptly felled more than 430 trees at the public East Potomac Golf Links for President Trump’s golf-course overhaul. On November 5, the National Capital Planning Commission votes on the President’s 250-foot vanity arch along the DCA approach path. The final plans for the arch do not appear to include the “top grade Military Complex” President Trump claimed to justify his gaudy, unserious plan, and I am still awaiting answers from the FAA and DoD to my September 25, 2026, questions about the President’s flippant use of the military to justify his ego-driven projects. When former President Obama likened the President’s gilded White House renovations to a Cheesecake Factory, official White House accounts and a Cabinet Secretary rushed to defend the décor within 48 hours. This administration moves with urgency when the President’s taste is questioned but with none when the American people struggle with the soaring cost of living or the NTSB warns of a “continued and unacceptable risk to public safety.”

Accordingly, I request written responses to the following questions:

Secretary Hegseth: On what date did the approval process begin for the October 29, 2026, flyover, who requested the mission, and what did the approval documents state as its purpose? Who was responsible for approving the flyovers? What was the justification for approval? Was the flight logged as a training sortie, and if so, what training objective did it fulfill?

Administrator Bedford: When was the FAA first notified of the flyovers, and how did that compare to the standard lead time for flyovers in the Flight Restricted Zone? What minimum altitude did the FAA authorize, what altitude did the aircraft actually fly, and was any deviation granted? Was a Notice to Airmen (NOTAM) issued? If so, when? Did anyone at FAA raise safety objections to the flyover? Did FAA evaluate the cost of delays to airlines and passengers?

Administrator Bedford and Secretary Hegseth: When were the DCA tower, Potomac Consolidated TRACON, the Metropolitan Washington Airports Authority, the airlines, and D.C.’s Mayor, Council and emergency management officials notified? Were the post-2009 notification procedures and transparency protocols followed for the flight? Who decided the public would receive only 15 minutes’ notice? How long did the ground stop last, and will you commit that no future ceremonial flyover of the NCR will proceed without at least 48 hours’ public notice?

Secretary Hegseth, Director Vought and Administrator Bedford: Secretary Hegseth, please provide a complete accounting of the cost to taxpayers—fuel, aircrew, maintenance and any support aircraft. Director Vought, please identify the appropriations accounts charged and any Office of Management and Budget review that applied. Administrator Bedford, please provide the cost of reviewing the flyover and any additional cost borne by the FAA.

Administrator Bedford and Secretary Hegseth: Please provide the status and projected completion date of each open NTSB recommendation from the January 29, 2025, collision, and of the FAA–DoD memorandum of understanding for the NCR.

Please provide accurate, honest and detailed written responses no later than November 20, 2026. On October 29, 2026, the country got a trick dressed up as a treat—and another reminder that this unserious President is more interested in impressing children with his toys than in meeting the needs of the American people.

title: Fetterman Statement in Support of Coca-Cola Teamsters Local 110 Strike
text:
BRADDOCK, PA — In announcing his support for the Teamsters Union Local 110 members who are on strike at the Abarta Coca Cola Plants in Cambria and Clearfield Counties, U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) today released the following statement:

“I’m proud to stand with the Teamsters Local 110 and every union member fighting for fair wages and a safe workplace. I urge Abarta Coca-Cola management to come back to the table and work together to create a fair deal for everyone.”

“The company did not want to bargain in good faith, we gave them several proposals and they simply said no and left. We filed a ULP. They would not counter. We tried to tell them what it would take to get it passed and they said we will not reward the behavior of striking. They now said they will not come back to the table till January of 2027 they will just hire replacements because sales are up 6% and they will be fine. These members are the lowest paid and pay the highest amount in health care in comparison to Greensburg and Houston facilities,” said Darrell Watt, President of Teamsters Local 110.

Teamsters Local 110 have been in negotiations with Abarta Coca-Cola since July and have been on strike for 10 days. The union members have rejected two contract proposals due to concerns over increases in healthcare costs and unfair wages. As of now, Local 110 leadership are waiting for Abarta Coca-Cola to return to the table and continue negotiations.

title: Gallego, Colleagues Demand Census Bureau Rescind Proposed Rule That Violates Constitution
text:
WASHINGTON – Senator Ruben Gallego (D-AZ) joined Senators Gary Peters (D-MI), Andy Kim (D-NJ), and a bipartisan group of 23 of their colleagues in demanding the U.S. Census Bureau rescind a proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from census counts and eliminate questions on race and ethnicity.

In their letter, the senators warn that the exclusion of non-citizens violates the Constitution, which expressly says that the census must count the “whole number of persons in each state.” The Census Bureau has proposed two methods by which it would exclude non-citizens, both of which would cause undercounts and errors in the census counts.

“We write to urge that you rescind your proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from decennial census counts and omit questions about race and ethnicity from the decennial census. The proposed rule violates the clear meaning of the Constitution, which requires that the Census Bureau count the ‘whole number of persons in each state.’ The proposed rule would also cause communities across the country to be counted inaccurately, jeopardizing their fair representation in Congress and access to billions of federal dollars for education, health care, and public safety services,” the senators wrote.

The letter also describes how the Bureau’s proposal to eliminate race and ethnicity questions would undermine the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws and would degrade the quality of all census data. Businesses and local governments that depend on such data have said that they would be harmed by this proposed rule.

“In its attempt to undermine the data used for the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws, the Bureau will degrade the accuracy of all other federal survey data, particularly for small and rural geographic areas. The Bureau writes in its own regulatory filing that the proposed rule ‘deteriorates the accuracy’ of ‘fertility/mortality rates, cancer rates, poverty rates, unemployment rates, [and] labor force participation’ because the Bureau relies on accurate decennial census information to adjust and design other survey estimates,” the senators continued. “The Bureau also admits in its filing that the proposal would hamper the usability of data for state and local governments who rely on precise and accurate population estimates for small geographic areas. Businesses and local governments that depend on reliable and complete federal data have warned that the Census Bureau’s proposal would increase costs as data is degraded.”

Joining Senators Gallego, Peters, and Kim in sending the letter were Senators Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Angus King (D-ME), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Patty Murray (D-WA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

title: Grassley Welcomes Over $76.2 Million in Federal Funding to Support Safety and Repair of Iowa Roads
text:
BUTLER COUNTY, IOWA – U.S. Sen. Chuck Grassley (R-Iowa) welcomed news from the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) that Iowa will receive over $76.2 million in federal funding to improve roadway safety across the state. This funding will impact Iowans in Palo Alto, Dubuque, Polk, Dallas, Warren, Hancock, Cerro Gordo, Franklin, Humboldt, Kossuth, Winnebago, Worth, Wright, Van Buren, Pottawattamie, Cedar, Jones, Muscatine and Washington counties. The funding will be administered through DOT’s Safe Streets and Roads for All program, which was established in the Grassley-backed Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA).

“Iowa families and manufacturers depend on the safety and reliability of our roads for everyday work and travel. I voted for the bipartisan infrastructure law with Iowans’ future in mind, and now 76 million more dollars are flowing to our state as a result. This federal funding will better connect our communities and keep Iowans safe,” Grassley said.

Details on the DOT awards follow:

Old Lincoln Highway Corridor Safety Project (Pottawattamie County): $19,900,000 to implement systemic safety improvements along 11.6 miles of Old Lincoln Highway between Sumac Road and Coit Road. The project addresses a documented corridor-wide pattern of severe lane-departure and run-off-road crashes on a high-risk corridor with 121 crashes between 2019 and 2023, including four fatal crashes and eight serious injury crashes.

Iowa Rural Roads Safety Initiative (Cedar, Jones, Muscatine, and Washington Counties): $11,600,000 to implement the Iowa Rural Road Safety Initiative on three high-risk rural corridors identified in each county’s Action Plan. Improvements on these corridors will include installation of four-foot paved shoulders with Safety Edge, centerline and edgeline rumble strips, enhanced pavement markings and curve delineation across 27 total miles on County Road X40, Garfield Avenue and Vine Avenue.

Mobilizing for Safety (Des Moines Area Metropolitan Planning Operation): $14,832,000 to implement nine roadway safety projects across the region that address speeding, failure to yield and pedestrian crossing risk on the high-injury network and high-risk network. The program includes two roundabouts, three pedestrian underpasses and four intersection and pedestrian enhancement projects.

Road to Zero: Van Buren County Rural Roads Safety Project: $7,280,000 to implement Action Plan-identified safety improvements along 9.7 miles of the Route V64 corridor between J40 and Highway 16, including eight high-risk curves and two high-risk intersections.

Northern Iowa Roadway Safety Improvements (Cerro Gordo, Franklin, Hancock, Humboldt, Kossuth, Palo Alto, Winnebago, Worth, and Wright Counties): $7,088,000 to implement 15 rural roadway safety projects at six segments, five curves and four intersections.

Adel Highway 169 Safety Corridor Improvement Project: $6,350,400 to reconstruct approximately one mile of U.S. Highway 169 from Greenwood Hill Drive to 302nd Street from a two-lane rural section to a three-lane urban roadway with a two-way left-turn lane. The project will address a Priority Corridor on the high-injury network where roadway design, 55 mile-per-hour operating conditions, and increasing school and local traffic create elevated risk for turning conflicts and severe crashes.

Polk County Communications Upgrade for Roadway Crash Response: $5,293,960 to upgrade public safety communications infrastructure that supports roadway crash response, traffic incident management and post-crash care across Polk County.

Dubuque SMART Safe Corridors Initiative: $3,443,040 to support traffic management system through rail crossing monitoring, predictive blockage analytics, emergency vehicle routing and signal preemption integration, expanded vulnerable road user detection, traveler information alerts and evaluation to inform future regional deployment.

Palo Alto County Post-Crash Care and Emergency Transport Risk Reduction Initiative: $415,711 to improve rural post-crash care after serious roadway crashes. The project will equip ambulances serving Palo Alto County with advanced monitoring, prehospital blood administration capability and point-of-care ultrasound to test trauma-care tools, improve field decision-making and inform future rural EMS and post-crash care initiatives countywide.

title: SIGNED INTO LAW: U.S. Senators Maggie Hassan and Katie Britt’s Clergy Act to Support America’s Faith Leaders
text:
WASHINGTON — Bipartisan legislation led by U.S. Senators Maggie Hassan and Katie Britt (R-AL) to support faith leaders who want to opt back into Social Security was recently signed into law. The Clergy Act, will allow clergy members who previously opted out of Social Security a time-limited opportunity to opt back in to coverage.

“I’m pleased to see our bipartisan Clergy Act signed into law. Clergy are important members of communities across New Hampshire, who help lead their congregation and provide comfort for Granite Staters during quiet moments and in difficult times,” said Senator Hassan. “This commonsense measure will allow clergy to opt back into Social Security and help them to safeguard their financial future and plan for a dignified retirement.”

Prior to this law, certain members of the clergy could make a one-time, irreversible decision to exempt their ministerial earnings from self-employment taxes. If they elected to do so, they would not receive Social Security and Medicare benefits based on that income.

Most clergy members are automatically covered by Social Security, but those who are conscientiously opposed may exempt themselves. Opting out excuses them from paying Social Security taxes and makes them ineligible for benefits, a decision often made early in their careers that some come to regret.

The Clergy Act will give these faith and community leaders a two-year re-enrollment window to opt back into Social Security coverage. Consistent with current eligibility requirements, clergy members who opt back in will generally need to earn 40 Social Security credits, typically requiring about 10 years of covered work, to qualify for Social Security retirement benefits. The bill will also require the IRS to develop and submit to Congress a plan to notify clergy members of their eligibility to revoke their exemptions.

Congress has repeatedly given clergy members who exempted themselves from Social Security the opportunity to opt back in, including in 1977, 1986, and most recently in 1999 through the Ticket to Work and Work Incentives Improvement Act.

title: Senator Hassan Highlights Efforts to Expand Mental Health and Addiction Care, Support New Hampshire Businesses at Events Across the State
text:
NEW HAMPSHIRE – U.S. Senator Maggie Hassan made stops across New Hampshire this week to highlight efforts to expand access to mental health and addiction care, and support New Hampshire’s businesses driving innovation in aerospace, defense, and other advanced technologies.

On Monday, Senator Hassan delivered remarks at the Mental Health Center of Greater Manchester's annual celebration, where she recognized the organization's work to provide mental health care and support to Granite Staters.

“One of the things that I hear about the most from people in New Hampshire – whether they live in the North Country or in the southernmost populated parts of the state – is the challenges that they and their families have getting the mental health care that they need,” said Senator Hassan. “The Mental Health Center of Greater Manchester is doing tremendous work to help address these challenges and ensure that more Granite Staters can get the care and support that they need.”

Senator Hassan speaks at the Mental Health Center of Greater Manchester's annual celebration

On Tuesday, Senator Hassan spoke at the Northeast Space, Technology, Trade and Research Expo Reception at the University of New Hampshire in Durham, where she met with industry leaders and researchers working in fields like aerospace, defense, robotics, and other advanced technologies. During her remarks, the Senator highlighted New Hampshire's long history of innovation and the important role that Granite State businesses play in creating good-paying jobs, developing new technologies, and strengthening national security. She also discussed the challenges that rising costs and President Trump's tariffs pose to New Hampshire manufacturers.

“Throughout our history, New Hampshire has continually reinvented its economy, adapting to world events and economic change, and finding new ways to pioneer advances in manufacturing,” said Senator Hassan. “What's behind our state's economic success? What makes New Hampshire different? It's our creativity, yes; also our ability to work together, and our resiliency and toughness. But behind all of that is one common thread responsible for our success: it's our love of freedom. It's our Live Free or Die spirit. That's what makes New Hampshire exceptional.”

On Wednesday, Senator Hassan spoke at the ribbon cutting for Hope for NH Recovery's new Pivot Program in Manchester, which will provide short-term housing and support for Granite Staters experiencing addiction, mental health crises, or homelessness. The new program will provide a safe place for individuals in crisis to stay while they work with staff to find longer-term care and resources.

“A common theme that I hear is about people who are struggling to get the help that they need when they are experiencing a crisis. Whether it's an addiction crisis, whether it is a mental health crisis, whether people find themselves without a safe place to call home, this is what the Pivot program is here to address,” said Senator Hassan. “The Pivot program is a testament to the progress and to the determination of everybody in this room and in the recovery community, especially the peer support community, which is critically important to people as they work hard to build a better future.”

Senator Hassan speaks at the ribbon cutting of Hope for New Hampshire Recovery’s Pivot Program

title: Warner and Kaine Statement On New Report Showing Effects On Virginia Of Infrastructure Law’s Expiration
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — Today, U.S. Senators Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) issued the following statement after a new report from the Senate Commerce Committee showed the effect that President Donald Trump’s refusal to work to reauthorize the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law—which Warner and Kaine helped negotiate and pass in 2021—will have on infrastructure projects throughout Virginia:

“Infrastructure should be an area in which both parties can find common ground, and as a matter of fact, we did: in 2021, we helped get the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law passed. But so far, the Trump-Vance Administration has refused to work in a bipartisan way to reauthorize that landmark legislation, meaning Virginia is facing millions of dollars in cuts to crucial infrastructure projects. Trump’s tariff policies and war of choice with Iran have sent prices for everything from building materials to gasoline through the roof—the last thing anyone needs now is for job-creating, economy-boosting infrastructure projects to dry up. Trump and the GOP can either come to the table and work with Democrats on reauthorizing this historic legislation, or infrastructure will join the long list of broken promises from the Trump-Vance Administration.”

According to the report from the Senate Commerce Committee, the expiration of the BIL will lead to more than 50 infrastructure projects in Virginia going unfunded, including 16 freight and rail projects and 40 roadway projects. The BIL has been delivering for Virginia, much like it has for the rest of the country, with nearly 100 transportation projects receiving funding from fiscal years 2022­–2026. The legislation must be reauthorized by December 11, 2026, or cuts to these programs may become permanent.

title: Warner, Kaine Announce $8.8 Million In Federal Funding To Improve Rail Crossing Safety Across Virginia
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Mark R. Warner and Tim Kaine (both D-VA) announced $8,810,502 in federal funding for four projects to improve railroad crossing safety, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen the movement of people and goods across Virginia. The funding was made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which the senators helped negotiate and pass.

“Safe and reliable rail transportation is essential to keeping Virginia families, businesses, and our economy moving,” said the senators. “These federal investments will improve safety at railroad crossings, cut down on traffic delays, and help goods travel more efficiently across the Commonwealth. We’re thrilled to see the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law continuing to deliver for Virginia communities.”

The funding will support the following projects:

$3,520,000 for the Portlock Road Grade Separation Project in Chesapeake to support final design work for the elimination of a railroad crossing along the Norfolk Southern rail corridor. The project will improve safety for drivers and pedestrians, reduce delays for emergency responders, and help freight move more efficiently to and from the Port of Virginia.

$2,000,000 for the U.S. Route 15 Railroad Overpass Improvements Project in Haymarket to support environmental review and preliminary engineering for a future grade separation at a highway-rail grade crossing at U.S. Route 15 and the Norfolk Southern B-line. The project will eliminate a crossing frequently blocked by trains, reducing traffic delays, improving emergency response times, and enhancing safety along a key commuter and freight corridor.

$1,719,342 for the Hampton Roads Transportation Planning Organization Grade Crossing Project in Chesapeake to support planning and safety evaluations of approximately 35 public highway-rail grade crossings along a major freight corridor serving the Port of Virginia. The project will identify opportunities to eliminate or separate crossings and improve safety technology in coordination with Norfolk Southern Railway and the Norfolk & Portsmouth Belt Line Railroad, as well as reduce traffic disruptions, strengthen access for emergency responders, and support freight movement through one of the nation’s busiest port complexes.

$1,571,160 for the Spotsylvania County Rail Safety Corridor Project to support final design work for safety improvements at three highway-rail grade crossings along the Richmond, Fredericksburg, and Potomac rail corridor. Planned improvements include separating Landsdowne Road from the railroad, upgrading warning devices at Mine Road, and installing active warning devices at Benchmark Road to reduce the risk of collisions and improve safety for motorists.

This funding was awarded through the Department of Transportation’s Railroad Crossing Elimination (Crossing Safety) Grant Program, which supports projects to eliminate dangerous rail crossings, improve transportation safety, reduce traffic delays, and strengthen the movement of people and goods. Each project will also be supported by a 20 percent non-federal cost share from local or regional partners.

Warner and Kaine have secured hundreds of millions of dollars in federal funding to modernize Virginia’s transportation infrastructure. Earlier this month, the senators announced $3.6 million to modernize the Shenandoah Valley Railroad. In August, the senators announced more than $17 million in federal funding for passenger rail improvement projects across Virginia, and in July, the senators announced more than $76 million for Virginia transportation infrastructure projects. Many of the investments were made possible by the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, a transformative investment in American infrastructure needs.

title: Kennedy applauds major federal investment for East Baton Rouge Parish to fight violent crime
text:
WASHINGTON – Sen. John Kennedy (R-La.), a member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, applauded the Department of Justice’s (DOJ) selection of East Baton Rouge Parish as one of just four jurisdictions nationwide to receive federal funding through its Model Cities Initiative (MCI), a nearly $300 million effort to fight violent crime, strengthen law enforcement and improve public safety.

“When our heroes in blue don’t have the resources to solve violent crimes, families pay the price. This is a huge win for Baton Rouge and Louisiana and will give law enforcement the tools they need to put violent criminals where they belong: behind bars,” said Kennedy.

The DOJ will award nearly $300 million collectively through the Model Cities Initiative to East Baton Rouge Parish and three other jurisdictions nationwide. The initiative takes a whole-of-city-approach to reducing crime and restoring law and order by bringing together law enforcement agencies, local government officials and community partners to address local public safety challenges.

The Model Cities Initiative funding will support:

Hiring and retaining law enforcement and other public safety personnel to strengthen violent crime investigations, enforcement and prosecution efforts.

Improving law enforcement technology to fight crime, including real-time crime centers, forensic and DNA tools, body-worn cameras, license plate readers, ballistic identification systems and information technology upgrades.

Training law enforcement personnel to strengthen intelligence-led policing, violent crime investigations, crisis response and coordination with state and federal law enforcement partners.

Improving public safety facilities, including training facilities, real time crime centers, intelligence analysis centers and other facilities used for public safety operations.

Expanding mental health and substance use services focused on prevention, crisis response, early intervention, treatment and other needs linked to public safety.

Strengthening reentry and recidivism reduction programs to reduce repeat offenses and help individuals successfully transition from custody back into their communities.

Expanding services for crime victims, including emergency assistance, temporary housing, medical care, advocacy, transportation and legal services.

Preventing youth crime and violence through juvenile crime prevention, intervention and gang suppression programs.

The DOJ will work with East Baton Rouge Parish to finalize and implement its public safety plan.

Background:

In May 2026, Kennedy and Sen. Booker (D-N.J.) reintroduced the bipartisan Violent Incident Clearance and Technological Investigative Methods (VICTIM) Act to give state, local and tribal law enforcement additional resources, personnel, training and technology to solve homicides and firearm-related offenses.

In January 2026, Kennedy secured several Department of Justice investments for Louisiana, including $2.195 million for Tangipahoa Parish’s Emergency Mobile Command Center, $1.5 million the Ruston Police Department, $794,000 for the West Monroe Police Department and $675,000 for the Louisiana Bureau of Investigation’s Internet Crimes Against Children Task Force.

title: Senators Kim and Peters Lead Senate Colleagues in Demanding Census Bureau Rescind Proposed Rule That Violates Constitution
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Andy Kim (D-NJ), Ranking Member of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee’s Subcommittee on the Census, and Gary Peters (D-MI), Ranking Member of the full Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs, led a bipartisan group of 24 colleagues urging the U.S. Census Bureau to rescind a proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from census counts and eliminate questions on race and ethnicity.

In their letter, the Senators warn that the exclusion of non-citizens violates the Constitution, which expressly says that the census must count the “whole number of persons in each state.” The Bureau has proposed two methods by which it would exclude non-citizens, both of which would cause undercounts and errors in the census counts.

“We write to urge that you rescind your proposed rule that would exclude certain non-citizens from decennial census counts and omit questions about race and ethnicity from the decennial census. The proposed rule violates the clear meaning of the Constitution, which requires that the Census Bureau count the ‘whole number of persons in each state.’ The proposed rule would also cause communities across the country to be counted inaccurately, jeopardizing their fair representation in Congress and access to billions of federal dollars for education, health care, and public safety services,” the senators wrote.

The letter also describes how the Bureau’s proposal to eliminate race and ethnicity questions would undermine the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws and would degrade the quality of all census data. The compliance of civil and voting rights laws rely on demographic data, and only the decennial census provides accurate and precise data. Additionally, eliminating the collection of race and ethnicity data from the decennial census undermines other federal survey data. Businesses and local governments that depend on such data have said that they would be harmed by this proposed rule.

“In its attempt to undermine the data used for the enforcement of civil and voting rights laws, the Bureau will degrade the accuracy of all other federal survey data, particularly for small and rural geographic areas. The Bureau writes in its own regulatory filing that the proposed rule ‘deteriorates the accuracy’ of ‘fertility/mortality rates, cancer rates, poverty rates, unemployment rates, [and] labor force participation’ because the Bureau relies on accurate decennial census information to adjust and design other survey estimates,” the senators continued. “The Bureau also admits in its filing that the proposal would hamper the usability of data for state and local governments who rely on precise and accurate population estimates for small geographic areas. Businesses and local governments that depend on reliable and complete federal data have warned that the Census Bureau’s proposal would increase costs as data is degraded.”

The full text of the letter is available here.

Joining Senators Kim and Peters in sending the letter were Senators Chuck Schumer (D-NY), Lisa Murkowski (R-AK), Tammy Baldwin (D-WI), Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), Catherine Cortez Masto (D-NV), Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), John Fetterman (D-PA), Ruben Gallego (D-AZ), Kirsten Gillibrand (D-NY), Maggie Hassan (D-NH), Martin Heinrich (D-NM), Mazie Hirono (D-HI), Mark Kelly (D-AZ), Angus King (I-ME), Jeff Merkley (D-OR), Patty Murray (D-WA), Jack Reed (D-RI), Jacky Rosen (D-NV), Brian Schatz (D-HI), Elissa Slotkin (D-MI), Chris Van Hollen (D-MD), Raphael Warnock (D-GA), Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), and Ron Wyden (D-OR).

title: Sens. Markey, Warren, Reps. McGovern, Trahan Statement on Amazon’s Withdrawal of Application to Operate Delivery Drone Program in Central Mass.
text:
Boston (November 2, 2026) - Senators Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), and Elizabeth Warren (D-Mass.), and Representatives Jim McGovern (MA-02), and Lori Trahan (MA-03) released the following statement after Amazon announced withdrawal of its application to launch autonomous delivery drones in Central Massachusetts after the lawmakers joined local communities in raising concerns about the Amazon Prime Air drone delivery program’s impact on the environment and residents’ quality-of-life, including noise pollution, health and safety, and privacy.

“We are glad that following our advocacy, and that of the State Legislative Delegation and local communities in Westborough and surrounding areas, Amazon has withdrawn its application to launch and operate autonomous delivery drones in Central Massachusetts at this time. Communities deserve a say in what happens in their neighborhoods, whether it is on the ground or in the sky, and especially when it comes to matters of quality-of-life, environmental protection, privacy, and public safety. We will continue to closely monitor drone delivery proposals, and make sure residents have a seat at the table.”

On October 14, the lawmakers wrote to Bryan Bedford, Administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), and Andy Jassy, Chief Executive Officer of Amazon, urging Amazon to work with the FAA to conduct an Environmental Assessment of its proposed drone delivery facility in Westborough, Massachusetts, before launching operations there.

title: Bonamici, Wyden, Merkley Demand Investigation into ICE Tire Slashing Incident
text:
WASHINGTON, DC [11/2/26] – Today Congresswoman Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01) and Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley demanded an investigation into Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents for slashing a couple’s tires in Hillsboro.

The couple was observing and recording ICE agents in a supermarket parking lot on October 7, 2026, before multiple masked ICE agents in three vehicles tailed the couple, boxed them in, and repeatedly stabbed and slashed their tires before driving away. A video of the incident can be viewed here.

“ICE agents cannot act with impunity,” the lawmakers wrote. “The First Amendment protects the right to observe, gather information, and record law enforcement officers performing their duties in public. These constitutional protections are necessary for the public to learn about and freely debate the government’s actions, including potential misconduct, and demand accountability when necessary.”

The lawmakers noted that there have been many documented cases of excessive use of force and intimidation tactics against peaceful community members and legal observers by ICE in Oregon and across the country. They called for the Inspector General for the Department of Homeland Security to immediately investigate the Oct. 7 incident in Hillsboro, identify the agents involved, and preserve all evidence, so that those responsible may be disciplined.

“Without videos from bystanders, observers, journalists, and protestors, the public would never know the full scale of federal retaliation against those who seek to document ICE activity,” the lawmakers wrote.

Bonamici, Wyden, Merkley, and Dexter also recently raised concerns about the lack of access to counsel for individuals detained by ICE and what appear to be new protocols for bypassing the Portland ICE facility entirely. That letter can be found here.

The full letter about the Oct. 7 incident can be read here and below:

Dear Inspector General Cuffari:

We write to request an investigation into an alarming incident that occurred on October 7, 2026, in which U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) agents harassed, intimidated, and retaliated against a couple in Hillsboro, Oregon for engaging in First Amendment activities. The incident occurred when our constituents observed and recorded ICE agents in a supermarket parking lot. Soon thereafter, multiple masked ICE agents in three vehicles recklessly tailed the couple, boxed them in, and dangerously vandalized their vehicle by repeatedly stabbing and puncturing one of their tires before driving away.1

ICE agents cannot act with impunity. The First Amendment protects the right to observe, gather information about, and record law enforcement officers performing their duties in public.2 These constitutional protections are necessary for the public to learn about and freely debate the government’s actions, including potential misconduct, and demand accountability when necessary.

Since President Trump returned to office in January 2025, federal ICE agents across the country have repeatedly failed to respect rights afforded under the Constitution, especially the First Amendment. We have seen many documented cases of excessive use of force and intimidation tactics by ICE in Oregon, including federal agents needlessly deploying tear-gas and other projectiles against peaceful community members as well as driving erratically and verbally threatening legal observers. This pattern of irresponsible and illegal behavior from federal agents is also evident across the country. For example, federal agents in Memphis, Tennessee harassed observers by swerving at them, tailing them, boxing them in, and pulling them over without reasonable suspicion; sitting outside of their homes; and assaulting and arresting them.3 In Los Angeles, federal agents fired crowd control weapons into the heads and other sensitive areas of observers, journalists, and protestors. A judge later granted an injunction against this behavior4 and found that the plaintiffs have plausibly alleged that DHS had a policy of retaliating against people who record the activities of agents.5

Most troubling, federal immigration agents killed Alex Pretti while he was peacefully recording and protesting ICE’s actions.6 Through all of this, the Trump administration has repeatedly covered up officer misconduct and obstructed investigations.7 To this day, there is no evidence that the federal government has meaningfully investigated Mr. Pretti’s killing, with his parents noting that “at every turn, they have ignored us, misled us and shielded Alex’s killers.”8 This reckless behavior and senseless violence endangers everyone across the country and does not advance ICE’s mission of enforcing immigration laws to preserve national security and public safety.

Without videos from bystanders, observers, journalists, and protestors, the public would never know the full scale of federal retaliation against those who seek to document ICE activity.

We hereby demand that your offices immediately undertake an investigation of the October 7, 2026, incident in Hillsboro, Oregon outlined above. Please identify the ICE agents involved and preserve all relevant evidence so the officers can be disciplined and prosecuted as appropriate.

Further, we request that you undertake a comprehensive investigation of the pervasive pattern of ICE agents acting unlawfully and retaliating against individuals exercising their First Amendment rights. We ask that you work with Congress to make lasting changes to ICE training, oversight, and accountability. The rights of our constituents must not be jeopardized any longer.

Sincerely,

###

title: Oregon Delegation Celebrates Federal Support for Oregon’s Hazelnut, Seafood Industries
text:
Washington, D.C. – Today, Oregon’s U.S. Senator Jeff Merkley led Oregon Congressional Delegation members—including Senator Ron Wyden and U.S. Representatives Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), Val Hoyle (OR-04), Andrea Salinas (OR-06), Maxine Dexter (OR-03), and Janelle Bynum (OR-05)—to announce that after pressure from the delegation, the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) will purchase hazelnuts and Pacific Whiting fillets under the agency’s Section 32 purchase program. These purchases will benefit communities and rural economies across Oregon by supporting domestic production and distribution of these agricultural goods during periods of significant market disruption and economic uncertainty.

“Our fisheries and farms deliver incredible products all around the world and are the lifeblood of our communities,” said Merkley, who led the Oregon delegation in pressing USDA to include hazelnuts and whiting in its latest food purchase. “This announcement ensures Oregon’s harvesters, processors, and producers will receive critical financial assistance needed to continue operating and providing services here in Oregon and beyond. I am elated the USDA has decided to make these purchases—this is a win for communities across our state.”

“Iconic state industries like agriculture and fishing count on the U.S. Department of Agriculture to do its job and support Oregonians working hard to keep producing their world-class goods,” said Wyden. “I’m glad the full-court press from the delegation has unlocked this win for Oregonians fishing Pacific whiting and growing hazelnuts.”

“Oregonians know that hazelnuts and seafood are some of the state’s most popular and delicious products,” said Bonamici. “Our growers and producers work tirelessly and bolster the local economy. I’m glad the USDA is making this investment.”

“These investments from the USDA will support the people who harvest, process and bring Pacific Whiting fish and hazelnuts to market,” said Hoyle. “By putting Oregon fishermen and farmers first, we’re boosting our coastal and rural economies.”

“Oregon’s specialty crop growers are the backbone of our economy, but too many are struggling with rising costs and uncertain markets,” said Salinas. “In the Willamette Valley, generations of farmers have depended on the hazelnut industry for their livelihoods. That’s why I joined my colleagues in pushing USDA to purchase Oregon hazelnuts and Pacific whiting. These purchases will provide much-needed support for our growers and fishing communities while putting more Oregon-grown and Oregon-caught food onto kitchen tables. I’m proud we secured this win for Oregon producers, and I’ll keep fighting to make sure our specialty crop farmers have the markets and resources they need to succeed.”

“Oregon’s farmers and fishermen work hard to feed our communities, and they deserve a federal government that stands behind them,” said Dexter. “Our delegation pushed USDA to act, and these $34 million in purchases will support Oregon’s hazelnut growers and fishermen during a difficult economic stretch. This investment will help sustain local jobs, strengthen rural and coastal economies, and get nutritious food to families who need it.”

“Our farmers are putting in the work every day to keep Oregon families fed,” said Bynum. “And they’re not just helping put food on the table, they’re keeping money with our families, creating good jobs close to home, and giving people what they need to put down roots here in Oregon. Money back in our state and with our farmers is a win-win.”

Previously, Merkley and the Oregon delegation pressed the USDA to include Pacific whiting and Oregon hazelnuts, which account for 99 percent of hazelnuts produced in the United States, in this year’s Section 32 purchases. Following their efforts, the USDA announced it was purchasing $22 million in hazelnuts and $12 million in Pacific whiting.

title: Salinas, Bonamici, Merkley, Wyden Secure over $500,000 for Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District
text:
Tualatin, OR — Today, Congresswomen Andrea Salinas (OR-06) and Suzanne Bonamici (OR-01), alongside Oregon Senators Ron Wyden and Jeff Merkley, announced they secured the release of over $530,000 in federal funding from the Natural Resources Conservation Service (NRCS) to support Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District (TSWCD).

In 2022, TSWCD applied to the NRCS for funding to improve fish habitat in Washington County. This work included replacing deteriorated culverts with bridges and modern culverts that help threatened species like steelhead trout move through local waterways. In February 2024, NRCS approved and obligated $1,074,887 to reimburse TSWCD for their work.

As of early September 2026, NRCS had only paid $543,837 of the over $1.07 million they had promised to TSWCD. This $531,000 shortfall has severely challenged TSWCD’s budget and would have stuck the taxpayers of Washington County with the bill. Following outreach from the Oregon delegation, NRCS honored its commitment and released the final sum to TSWCD.

“When Oregonians make a promise, we keep it. The federal government should be held to the same standard,” said Rep. Salinas. “Tualatin Soil and Water did the work to improve our waterways, and Washington County taxpayers should never have been left holding the bag. I’m glad we got this money out the door and where it belongs.”

“Supporting threatened species and their habitats reflects Oregon values and our commitment to environmental protection, and I was grateful when the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District secured federal funds to improve fish habitat in Washington County,” said Rep. Bonamici. “Unfortunately, the Trump administration paid only about half of the promised funding, leaving Washington County taxpayers to pick up the balance. I’m glad that my colleagues and I were able to help resolve this issue and secure all the funds the water conservation district needed for the project.”

“Thanks to our efforts, this funding is finally moving forward and will help ensure the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District can continue its work to improve waterways in Washington County,” said Sen. Merkley. “Oregon’s native fish are the lifeblood of our state, supporting the health and vitality of our communities, local economies, and Tribes who have been here since time immemorial. I’ll keep pushing to secure the necessary federal funds to protect our state’s ecosystems for generations to come.”

“I’m glad the full-court press by the delegation unlocked these resources promised by the federal government to the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District,” Wyden said. “These funds will keep waterways improvements on track, helping with water quality and fish habitat alike in Washington County.”

“The Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District much appreciates Congresswoman Salinas and her staff for their work in helping the District receive payment from the U.S. Department of Agriculture for a successful fish habitat project in the Gales Creek watershed of Washington County,” said Dean P. Moberg, Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District Treasurer. “We were impressed with the staff’s quick understanding of the payment problem we faced, and we are grateful for the Congresswoman’s exceptional response. The letter Congresswoman Salinas provided, along with Congresswoman Bonamici and Senators Merkley and Wyden, was surely instrumental in cutting through red tape and securing the payment of over one half million dollars in federal assistance that had been held up for this project. This payment will greatly facilitate the Tualatin Soil and Water Conservation District’s work in helping residents of Washington County conserve natural resources with voluntary and locally led projects.

This press release has been updated.

title: Warnock, Ossoff Secure Over $12 Million in Federal Funding to Repair Roadways Damaged by Natural Disasters
text:
Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff successfully secured over $12 million in federal funding from the Department of Transportation to repair and reconstruct roads damaged by natural disasters across Georgia

The funding is provided through the Federal Highway Administration Emergency Relief Program

The funding will support critical roadway repairs across Georgia, including in the Chattahoochee and Oconee National Forests, following damage caused by Hurricane Helene, Hurricane Rafael, and severe ice storms

Washington D.C. — U.S. Senators Reverend Raphael Warnock (D-GA) and Jon Ossoff (D-GA) secured over $12 million in federal funding to repair and reconstruct roads damaged by natural disasters across Georgia. The funding, provided through the U.S. Department of Transportation’s (DOT) Federal Highway Administration (FHWA) Emergency Relief Program, will support roadway repairs across Georgia, including in the Chattahoochee and Oconee National Forests, following damage caused by Hurricane Helene, Hurricane Rafael, and severe ice storms.

“Communities across our state have been through a lot in the wake of these devastating storms, and for many, the work of rebuilding is far from over,” said Senator Warnock. “This federal funding will help repair roads damaged by these storms and make sure Georgians can safely get where they need to go.”

“Bringing Republicans and Democrats together, we are delivering these resources to help improve Georgia’s roads and highways that were impacted after Hurricane Helene and other storms,” said Senator Ossoff.

The funding includes $8.9 million to repair roadways and drainage structures in the Chattahoochee and Oconee National Forests that were heavily damaged during severe ice storms earlier this year. The funding package also includes $2.3 million to address widespread damage to traffic signals, roadways, signs and sign structures that were impacted by Hurricane Helene. Nearly $841,000 will support communities in South and East Georgia where Hurricane Rafael caused several rivers to overflow their banks, flooding roadways, damaging culverts and causing washouts.
