title: Finstad Urges Trump Administration to Approve Disaster Declaration in Southeastern Minnesota
text:
ROCHESTER, MN – Congressman Brad Finstad (MN-01) joined U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tina Smith (D-MN) in urging President Donald Trump and his administration to approve the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance covering Fillmore, Houston, Steele, and Waseca Counties. The letter also calls for President Trump’s support of the Individuals and Households Program, Disaster Unemployment Assistance, and Hazard Mitigation assistance to invest in disaster resiliency efforts.

In September 2026, southeastern Minnesota experienced severe storms and flooding, leading to more than three-quarters of homes, as well as the New Richland Care Center, a skilled nursing care facility, being damaged. Joint federal and state emergency management teams conducted preliminary damage assessments and determined the losses have met the threshold for federal assistance under the Stafford Act through a Major Disaster Declaration.

The letter reads:

Dear Mr. President:

We write to you in strong support of the state of Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance under the Stafford Act to assist our constituents recovering from severe storms and flooding. These natural disasters have caused significant damage, and we ask that you quickly grant approval for federal disaster assistance.

In September 2026, south and southeastern Minnesota experienced severe weather events that caused flooding in the region. A line of thunderstorms formed late September 18 and repeatedly passed over the same communities into early September 19. Approximately 700 square miles across this region received six inches or more of precipitation within 24 hours, according to the Minnesota Department of Natural Resources. In the City of New Richland alone, more than three-quarters of homes are damaged and residents of a skilled nursing facility were evacuated and unable to return to the facility. Many homes across the impacted area suffered flooded basements and damaged furnaces and boilers which will need repair or replacement ahead of the Minnesota winter. This storm event has been assessed as at least as destructive as the July 2026 mega-rain that many of these communities experienced and were recovering from just months prior.

Joint federal and state emergency management teams have conducted preliminary damage assessments and have determined that the losses meet the threshold for federal assistance under the Stafford Act through a Major Disaster Declaration. Governor Walz has submitted an official request for disaster assistance for the period of September 18 to September 20, 2026. The request, dated November 2, 2026, covers Fillmore, Houston, Steele, and Waseca Counties.

Time and time again, Minnesotans have stepped up to support their neighbors after natural disasters. When flood waters rise and homes are damaged, volunteers and neighbors are quick to fill sandbags, clean up debris, and lend a hand to those in need. Impacted communities will repair the damage and rebuild following these disasters, but rapid federal assistance will speed up this recovery effort.

We strongly support Minnesota’s request for a Major Disaster Declaration for Individual Assistance, including for the Individuals and Households program and Disaster Unemployment Assistance, as well as Hazard Mitigation assistance to invest in disaster resiliency efforts. We ask that you grant its approval without delay.

Sincerely,

Amy Klobuchar, United States Senator

Tina Smith, United States Senator

Brad Finstad, Member of Congress

title: Rep. Nancy Mace Introduces the PURGE Act to Target Microplastics in America’s Waters
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C., (Nov. 6, 2026) – Today, Congresswoman Nancy Mace (R-SC) introduced the Plastics Understanding and Removal through Government Evaluation (PURGE) Act, legislation directing the Environmental Protection Agency to study and test strategies to remove microplastics from the environment and our water supply and prevent plastics from breaking down into persistent microplastic and nanoplastic particles.

Microplastics are present everywhere in the environment, including our rivers, oceans, and seafood. The PURGE Act demands answers. What works. What it costs. And whether it can be put to use at water treatment and environmental facilities.

The bill focuses on two approaches: removing microplastics already in our environment through filtration and capture, and engineering plastics to break down naturally instead of fragmenting into persistent microplastic and nanoplastic particles.

“Microplastics are in our water and on our dinner plates, and we have yet to know what actually works to stop them,” said Congresswoman Mace. “The PURGE Act puts the EPA to work finding real solutions, tested in the real world and measured by hard science. No more guessing. No gimmicks. Our families deserve a microplastic-free future, and we intend to deliver it.”

The PURGE Act:

Directs the EPA to study anti-microplastic strategies, including their effectiveness, cost, toxic byproducts, and impact on recycling, and report to Congress within 180 days.

Establishes a five-year pilot program testing these strategies in at least three different sites across diverse geographic regions, including riverine, coastal, and municipal wastewater settings to the extent practicable.

Requires the EPA to set measurable success standards before any testing begins.

Prioritizes solutions capable of working with existing water treatment and stormwater infrastructure, without substantial new construction.

Requires biodegradation to be verified through molecular-level testing, not visual inspection or mass-loss measurements alone.

Requires coordination with NOAA, the U.S. Geological Survey, and state environmental agencies.

Requires a final report to Congress on pilot results within one year of the program's conclusion.

title: Wall Street Journal Editorial Board: Mike Johnson’s Good House Service
text:
WASHINGTON — Read today’s editorial from the Wall Street Journal highlighting Speaker Johnson’s record: “Mike Johnson’s Good House Service.”

“The country owes a debt to the Congressman from Louisiana for taking on a nearly impossible job, and the country is the better for his influence,” the Editorial Board wrote.

Read the full WSJ Editorial here or below:

Mike Johnson’s Good House Service

The Editorial Board

Wall Street Journal

November 6, 2026

House Speaker Mike Johnson says he won’t run for Minority Leader after the Republican defeat this week, and Washington would be better if more politicians stepped aside with honor. But the country owes a debt to the Congressman from Louisiana for taking on a nearly impossible job, and the country is the better for his influence.

Mr. Johnson was hardly a household name in 2023 when a faction of House Republicans deposed Speaker Kevin McCarthy with no obvious replacement. The GOP descended into a circular firing squad that lasted weeks. The reserve currency in the panic turned out to be a constitutional lawyer with an aspirational politics and a Ronald Reagan worldview.

Mr. Johnson had to navigate an historically small majority and a President who never tried to persuade the public. He deserves particular credit for renewing the 2017 tax cuts, when failure was possible given divisions over state tax deductions and more. The One Big Beautiful Bill made progress on Medicaid sanity, higher education reform, work requirements and more. Mr. Johnson also helped move through the bipartisan bill on TikTok ownership that perhaps someday a President will follow.

He also deserves credit for his leadership moving military support for Ukraine, Taiwan and Israel, even over heckling from his own party. His speech at the Hudson Institute in the summer of 2024 should be required reading for Republicans trying to pick up the pieces after Mr. Trump.

“Today, we are threatened again by Chinese Communists, by Russian oligarchs, and Islamic terrorists,” he said. “We can choose to ignore them, we can try to appease them. We can listen to the naysayers who say our values aren’t worth defending and that there can be no victory. Or we can choose another course… We can rearm, rebuild, reinvigorate, restore, and reinstate fear in our enemies.”

The GOP Congress wasn’t as productive as we’d hoped, but Mr. Johnson wasn’t the problem. He had to navigate between a President with mercurial and often unrealistic demands and a backbench with too many podcasters and social-media trolls.

The Speaker is taking hits for predicting that Republicans would keep the House, but electoral optimism is a requirement of the job. The defeat wasn’t his fault. He raised record funds for candidates. The Speaker from Louisiana understood, as he likes to say quoting John Quincy Adams, that “duty is ours; results are God’s.”

title: Congressman Griffith’s Weekly E-Newsletter 11.6.26
text:
Veterans Day is an American tradition to honor those who have served in the armed forces of the United States. Their service is rooted in love of country and community.

These values not only shape the brave Americans who enlist in military service, but they also help guide our servicemembers who later become political leaders.

Throughout American history, some who take the oath to enlist in our military later take the presidential oath of office.

America’s first president under the Constitution, General George Washington, led the Continental Army in the fight against the British throne.

Responding to Supreme Court Chief Justice John Marshall’s biography of Washington, Gouverneur Morris, a contemporary of both, wrote to Marshall: “…few men of such steady, persevering industry ever existed, and perhaps no one who so completely commanded himself.”

Another military leader to fight Great Britain before pursuing the presidency was our 7th president and the first from the Democratic Party, Andrew Jackson.

In addition to receiving heavy praise for his role in the Battle of New Orleans, Jackson’s campaign to squash the Seminole created negotiating room for the U.S. to acquire Florida.

While Jackson’s military focus during the War of 1812 was in the South, American forces also had to respond to British attacks in the North.

William Henry Harrison, later America’s 10th president, commanded an army following the British capture of Detroit. Harrison pushed back British and Indian forces in a campaign that led to the recapture of Detroit and even the invasion of Ontario, Canada.

Harrison’s lead in Canada at the Battle of the Thames was considered one of the greatest American victories along with Jackson’s at New Orleans.

Unfortunately, Harrison served as president for just 31 days before his death, becoming the first president to die in office and remaining the shortest-serving president to this day.

The next president to die in office was another Virginia-born military leader, Zachary Taylor.

Taylor’s exceptional command during the Mexican-American War earned him major general honors, three Congressional Gold Medals (the only person in U.S. history) and comparisons to Washington and Jackson.

Serving under Taylor in the war effort was Ulysses S. Grant. The conflict helped shape Grant in his preparation to lead the Union Army during the Civil War.

Grant would later become our country’s first president elected following the Civil War, and the first since Jackson to complete two consecutive terms.

Among others to go from fighting in the Civil War to later living in the White House included the likes of Benjamin Harrison, James Garfield and William McKinley.

As the 25th president, McKinley helped exert American power in the Western Hemisphere, most notably during the Spanish-American War.

American forces showed incredible strength, with leaders like Teddy Roosevelt and his Rough Riders valiantly fighting in Cuba against Spanish armed forces.

Following Roosevelt’s resounding success in the War, he became a rising star in the Republican Party. Accordingly, McKinley tapped Roosevelt as his new vice president. McKinley’s assassination in 1901 meant the Spanish-American War hero would take the reins of the presidency, and in 1904, would be elected in his own right.

Another Republican war hero to become president is General Dwight D. Eisenhower.

Eisenhower, among other campaigns, oversaw the Allied operation in World War II, Operation Overlord, which is one of the most consequential military feats in U.S. military history. The Allied landings at Normandy, the largest seaborne invasion in history, represented the first major breach of Hitler’s “Fortress Europe” and paved the way for America and our Allies to defeat Nazi forces.

Across the world in the Pacific Theater, American forces faced a different threat.

Naval warfare against Japan required courageous aviators to bomb Japanese-held islands. One naval aviator, 19-year-old George Herbert Walker Bush, took on a variety of combat missions.

During one attack, Bush was shot down by enemy fire. He parachuted into the ocean, spending four hours on a life raft before being rescued.

Bush’s military service preceded his rise in public service, where he would become America’s 41st president.

These are just some of the many presidents to have a military service background.

America’s military leaders not only fight on the battlefield, but also on American soil to protect our rights, our way of life and our country.

Obviously, not all veterans can become president. But whether they become president or return to contribute to their communities, every American owes them a debt of gratitude. So, please join me in thanking our veterans for all they do and have done for our country. Happy Veterans Day!

If you have questions, concerns, or comments, feel free to contact my office. You can call my Abingdon office at 276-525-1405 or my Christiansburg office at 540-381-5671. To reach my office via email, please visit my website at https://morgangriffith.house.gov/.

title: Griffith Celebrates Opportunity Zone Designations in Virginia’s Ninth District
text:
The U.S. Department of Treasury approved Virginia’s nomination of 153 new Opportunity Zones (OZs) as proposed by Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger. A map of the new OZs in Virginia, which are set to take effect in January 2027, is available here.

The OZ program is meant to incentivize private investment capital in economically distressed communities. This federal initiative, which was permanently extended through the 2025 reconciliation bill, H.R. 1 - the Working Families Tax Cuts Act, now includes boosted tax incentives for OZs in rural communities. Capital gains placed into rural investments are subject to a discount three times that of non-rural investments. In addition, the investment threshold for improving a facility is reduced. U.S. Congressman Morgan Griffith (R-VA) voiced his support for boosted OZ tax incentives for rural communities as he voted in favor of the Working Families Tax Cuts Act.

In response to this announcement, Congressman Griffith released the following statement:

“As an original supporter of Opportunity Zones, this policy helps attract investments, generate economic growth and create jobs in communities that need it. In 2025, I supported the expansion of this program to allow more rural communities to potentially access private investment.

“Today’s announcement confirms that Virginia’s Ninth District will have more rural Opportunity Zones than any other Congressional District in Virginia.

“I am glad to have secured this outcome for our rural communities by voting for the Working Families Tax Cuts. I will continue to support policies that strengthen economic opportunity in rural America.”

BACKGROUND

According to the Economic Innovation Group, $1.9 billion in OZ investments supported Virginia communities through the end of 2024.

title: SALAZAR, BERA, GIMENEZ INTRODUCE BIPARTISAN BILL TO PROTECT TROPICAL FORESTS AND CORAL REEFS
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. — U.S. Representatives María Elvira Salazar (R-FL-27), Ami Bera (D-CA-06), and Carlos Gimenez (R-FL-28) introduced the bipartisan Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Reauthorization Act of 2026 (H.R. 10505), legislation to continue a longstanding U.S. conservation program that helps protect tropical forests and coral reef ecosystems around the world.

U.S. Senators Chris Coons (D-DE) and John Curtis (R-UT), introduced companion legislation in the Senate.

The legislation would reauthorize the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Act of 1998, which allows eligible developing countries to restructure certain debt owed to the United States while directing funds toward the protection and restoration of tropical forests and coral reefs.

Current law authorizes $20 million annually for the program through Fiscal Year 2027. H.R. 10505 would extend that authorization at $20 million per year from Fiscal Year 2028 through Fiscal Year 2032.

"In South Florida and across the globe, ecosystem protection and restoration are central not only to the well-being of wildlife but also play a critical role in boosting local economies," said Rep. Salazar. "By reauthorizing this proven program, we will continue to preserve native wildlife and ecosystems, help grow economies, and strengthen our alliances. I am proud to help lead this bipartisan effort and reinforce America’s leadership in conservation around the world.”

“Protecting tropical forests and coral reefs is essential to preserving biodiversity and protecting our environment for future generations,” said Representative Ami Bera, M.D. “Reauthorizing this funding will ensure we continue to protect and restore critical tropical forest and coral reef ecosystems whose health has far-reaching consequences for communities and economies around the world. I’m proud to join Representative Salazar in supporting this bipartisan effort to continue this vital conservation work.”

"Over the years the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Act has helped conserve areas rich with biodiversity," said Catherine Barrett, Legislative Director for The Nature Conservancy. "The law additionally paved the way for innovative conservation funding, leveraging public funding with private and philanthropic investments to benefit nature and people. The Nature Conservancy is grateful to Congresswoman Salazar and Congressman Bera for their bipartisan leadership in introducing this important reauthorization effort."

"Congresswoman Salazar and Congressman Bera are applauded for their leadership in introducing legislation in the House of Representatives to renew the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Reauthorization Act," said Kelly Keenan Aylward, Executive Director of Federal Affairs & Policy for the Wildlife Conservation Society. "This innovative policy converts eligible debt into long-term financing for on-the-ground conservation of intact forest, coral reefs, and wildlife while strengthening governance in the natural resource sector."

"The introduction of legislation in the U.S. House to reauthorize the Tropical Forest and Coral Reef Conservation Act is an important step toward unlocking innovative financing for the world’s most vulnerable tropical forests and coral reef ecosystems,” said Kerry Cesareo, senior vice president for forests and freshwater at World Wildlife Fund. “By strengthening this proven approach, we can help nations reduce debt burdens while investing in the natural systems that protect communities, support biodiversity and promote our prosperity. We welcome this bipartisan commitment to solutions that deliver lasting environmental and economic benefits.”

“Thanks to the leadership of then-Representative Rob Portman, and to the support of the International Conservation Caucus Co-Chairs in the Senate & House for the past 20 years, the Tropical Forest Conservation Act (now the Tropical Forest & Coral Conservation Act) is responsible for conserving 126,000,000 acres globally,” said David Barron, ICCF Group Chairman. “Debt-for-nature swaps are the best investment America could make in setting aside land for local people and their economies.”

The bill builds on Rep. Salazar’s record of advancing conservation and resilience efforts important to South Florida. Her bipartisan conservation work includes the REEF Act, which encourages retired Navy ships to be repurposed as artificial reefs, and the Migratory Birds of the Americas Conservation Enhancements Act, both signed into law.

Rep. Salazar has also secured federal investments for coral reef restoration, water quality, flood mitigation, and coastal resilience projects across Florida’s 27th Congressional District.

title: Reps. Vargas, Jacobs, Levin, Peters and Senators Padilla and Schiff Call for Answers and Investigation into Death at Otay Mesa
text:
SAN DIEGO – U.S. Representatives Juan Vargas (CA-52), Sara Jacobs (CA-51), Mike Levin (CA-49), and Scott Peters (CA-50) and U.S. Senators Alex Padilla (D-CA)and Adam Schiff (D-CA) called on the Trump Administration for answers following the death of an individual in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center. Together, the Members are demanding a thorough and transparent investigation into whether all policies, procedures, and standards of care were appropriately followed.

“As Members of the San Diego Congressional Delegation, we write to express our grave concern following the latest death of an individual in ICE custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center in San Diego, California, operated by the for-profit prison corporation CoreCivic,” wrote the lawmakers. “Any death in federal custody is a tragic reminder of the serious responsibility entrusted to DHS, ICE, and their contracted detention facilities, to safeguard the lives of those in their care.”

“A thorough investigation is all the more important in light of previously documented concerns regarding delayed access to medical care, subpar detention conditions, and compliance with public health reporting requirements,” the lawmakers continued. “We further request that the Department regularly update Members of Congress as the investigation progresses. Without complete and accurate information, Congress cannot fully assess whether existing policies, procedures, and safeguards are sufficient to protect individuals in federal custody.”

Read the full letter below:

Dear Secretary Mullin and Acting Director Venturella,

As Members of the San Diego Congressional Delegation, we write to express our grave concern following the latest death of an individual in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center in San Diego, California, operated by the for-profit prison corporation CoreCivic. This death underscores the importance of ensuring the safety and well-being of detainees in federal custody, particularly given the previously documented concerns about medical care and oversight at the facility.

On Saturday, October 24, a 43-year-old Guatemalan man, subsequently identified by San Diego County officials as Guillermo Pascual Verganza, died while in ICE custody at Otay Mesa Detention Center. ICE initially identified the individual as Roberto Jimenez Gutierrez, raising additional questions regarding the accuracy of the information released following his death. According to CoreCivic, facility staff reported a medical emergency at 11:36 a.m. after discovering Mr. Verganza unresponsive in his assigned living area. Although medical personnel reportedly initiated lifesaving measures and requested emergency medical services, he was pronounced dead before he could be transported from the facility. The cause and circumstances of his death remain under investigation and an autopsy was done on Monday, October 26. While we recognize that the facts and details of this case are still emerging, any death in federal custody warrants a thorough review to ensure that appropriate policies, procedures, and standards of care were followed. This includes examining the medical attention and monitoring provided to Mr. Verganza during his detention, as well as the circumstances of his placement in a safety cell and the facility’s response to the emergency.

Any death in federal custody is a tragic reminder of the serious responsibility entrusted to DHS, ICE, and their contracted detention facilities, to safeguard the lives of those in their care. A thorough investigation is all the more important in light of previously documented concerns regarding delayed access to medical care, subpar detention conditions, and compliance with public health reporting requirements. A California 2026 Department of Justice report identified concerns regarding medical recordkeeping, delays in treatment, and coordination of specialty care referrals and follow-up treatment. The report also documented concerns regarding detention conditions, including overcrowding and insufficient access to toilets in certain housing units.

Separately, a June 2026 San Diego County Health and Environmental Inspection Report, released in August, identified deficiencies in the facility's medical practices, particularly failures to appropriately report and coordinate tuberculosis cases with local public health authorities. County officials found that two tuberculosis cases were not reported by facility medical personnel and instead came to the attention of public health officials through an outside laboratory vendor. Individuals with tuberculosis require reporting within 24 hours and coordinated response as per Health and Safety Code Section 121361. The inspection also identified that no vaccines were stocked at the time of inspection and an individual who had gone 18 months without a replacement for a medically required dental or medical device.

While these findings do not establish that any deficiencies contributed to the recent death, they underscore the importance of a thorough and transparent investigation into the circumstances surrounding it. Given the seriousness of a detainee death, we request that the Department share with Members of Congress any relevant findings and information obtained through its investigation by Friday, November 13. We further request that the Department regularly update Members of Congress as the investigation progresses. Without complete and accurate information, Congress cannot fully assess whether existing policies, procedures, and safeguards are sufficient to protect individuals in federal custody.

###

title: Baldwin Releases Statement After Video Emerges of Railroad CEO Threatening Retaliation for Opponents of Megamerger
text:
WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senator Tammy Baldwin (D-WI) released a statement calling out Union Pacific CEO Jim Vena for threatening to raise rates on customers – including Wisconsin farmers, manufacturers, and businesses – who oppose the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern megamerger. In a newly released video, Vena told a room of rail shippers, “I’ll probably increase everybody’s rates that said they didn’t want a seamless railroad by three or four extra percent to teach you a lesson.”

Baldwin has warned for months that this merger will raise costs and worsen already poor rail service for American businesses and consumers. Senator Baldwin’s work to scrutinize this merger – in Senate testimony and public letters – led to federal regulators heeding her calls and ordering the video of Union Pacific’s threats of retaliation be made public. She has called on the Surface Transportation Board to reject the merger.

“For years, I’ve heard from Wisconsin businesses, farmers, and manufacturers about how consolidation in Class I rail has led to unreliable service and high costs that are passed onto Wisconsin families. That’s why I’ve called on the Trump Administration to reject this megamerger and protect American consumers, not the billionaire class and corporations who are just looking to stamp out competition and pad their profits,” said Senator Baldwin. “Today, we can see for ourselves that Union Pacific’s CEO is openly talking about retaliating against shippers who are rightfully concerned that more consolidation in Class I rail will lead to worse service and higher costs for businesses, farmers, and families. That’s no laughing matter to my constituents. I’m calling on the Surface Transportation Board to reject a megamerger that will hurt our Made in Wisconsin economy.”

In March 2026, reports emerged that Union Pacific (UP) CEO Jim Vena threatened retaliation at the Southwestern Association of Rail Shippers annual meeting with rate increases against shippers who oppose the merger. Following these reports, Senator Baldwin questioned Surface Transportation Board (STB) nominee Karen Hedlund about whether federal regulators would take these threats seriously. Hedlund stated that any kind of retaliation against shippers would be “utterly unacceptable.” Senator Baldwin followed up her questioning by calling on the STB to take Union Pacific’s threats seriously. Yesterday, the STB forced Union Pacific to make those remarks public.

Since the 1950s, the rail industry has consolidated from over 100 Class I freight railroads to only six today, leaving U.S. manufacturers, utility companies, agricultural producers, and small businesses paying excessive rates despite poor service and reliability. For months, Senator Baldwin has been urging federal regulators to thoroughly scrutinize this merger’s impact on competition, shipping costs, and service reliability for Made in Wisconsin businesses who rely on freight rail:

July 2025: Baldwin and Republican Senator Roger Marshall of Kansas urged the Surface Transportation Board (STB) to closely examine the proposed merger's impact on competition, costs, and reliability.

November 2025: During a Senate Commerce Committee nomination hearing, Baldwin pressed Surface Transportation Board member nominees Richard Kloster and Michelle Schultz on whether they would act independently of President Trump when making regulatory decisions.

December 2025: Senator Baldwin called on the STB to reject the merger application filed by Union Pacific to acquire Norfolk Southern.

June 2026: During a Senate Commerce Committee nomination hearing, Baldwin questioned STB nominee Karen Hedlund on CEO Jim Vena’s past comments. She also asked for clarification if Union Pacific could disregard its burden to prove the merger satisfies the public interest statute.

July 2026: Baldwin urged the Surface Transportation Board to take Union Pacific’s threat of retaliation against shippers who do not support its merger with Norfolk Southern seriously. Her letter came as Union Pacific’s CEO previously visited President Trump in the Oval Office and committed to helping fund the President’s $400 million White House ballroom.

title: Senator Blumenthal: Week in Review 10/30/2026-11/6/2026
text:
Warning Targets of Investigations Into Crypto Corruption, Immigration Abuses, Big Tech & More after Blue Wave Retakes Congress

[Hartford, CT] – U.S. Senator Richard Blumenthal (D-CT), incoming Chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations (PSI), issued a sweeping notice to individuals, companies, and government agencies that have failed to cooperate with a range of ongoing inquiries, including investigations into cryptocurrency; corruption involving the Trump Administration’s self-enrichment and national security threats; rampant misconduct by federal immigration agents; Big Tech and other corporate enablers; and the Trump Administration’s lawless abuse of power.

In a series of letters, Blumenthal reminded recipients of the Subcommittee’s expectation for their prompt cooperation and warned: “Please also note that failure to voluntarily produce the requested records and information by January 4, 2027, will leave the Subcommittee with no choice but to consider alternative measures to obtain compliance.”

The entities receiving letters include:

World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC: In May 2025, Blumenthal opened an inquiry into the $TRUMP cryptocurrency and World Liberty Financial Inc. (WLFI) following reporting that Trump-connected cryptocurrency firms may be enabling the violation of government ethics requirements, facilitating financial transactions with foreign nationals under federal prosecution, taking investments from foreign governments, and potentially violating federal laws. In July 2026, Blumenthal hosted a public forum on the Trump family’s crypto ventures, including publishing testimony from $TRUMP coin investors who lost thousands on the scheme. Blumenthal’s letter to World Liberty Financial is available here and Fight Fight Fight LLC is available here.

Binance and Tether: Blumenthal is leading an inquiry into the illicit use of cryptocurrencies and the Trump Administration’s self-enrichment and self-dealings with cryptocurrency firms. As part of this investigation, Blumenthal released a report detailing how Tether and its dollar-pegged stablecoin have become a significant financial lifeline within Iran’s shadow banking network. Blumenthal’s letter to Binance is available here and Tether is available here.

Secretary of Homeland Security Markwayne Mullin: In August 2025, Blumenthal opened an expansive inquiry into abuses by DHS and federal immigration enforcement authorities. Over the last two years, Blumenthal and U.S. Representative Robert Garcia (D-CA), Ranking Member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, have hosted five public forums to receive testimony from whistleblowers and victims about lawless and abusive tactics used by federal immigration agents. Blumenthal’s letter to Mullin is available here.

Tech companies and all other publicly known donors to the Trump Ballroom: Blumenthal is leading an inquiry into Big Tech companies and others who may be seeking pay-to-play government favors from their donations to President Trump’s White House ballroom and other projects throughout the nation’s capital. Blumenthal has repeatedly sought answers from private donors to the ballroom project as well as raised concerns to White House Chief of Staff Susie Wiles about the ballooning costs associated with renovations to the White House and surrounding grounds, including the multi-million-dollar cost to taxpayers. Blumenthal’s letters to all publicly known donors to the Trump Ballroom project are available here.

Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Chair Brendan Carr: In March 2025, Blumenthal opened an inquiry into the FCC’s abuse of power, including dubious investigations and misrepresentations of law to silence free speech. In September 2025, Blumenthal hosted a public forum with U.S. Senator Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) on the Trump Administration’s unprecedented efforts to use the FCC and government authority to chill First Amendment-protected speech and independent, fact-based news reporting. Blumenthal’s letter to Carr is available here.

Blumenthal further highlighted his warning to those that have failed to cooperate with a range of ongoing inquiries on Twitter/X.

“Targets of my investigations—immigration abuses, Big Tech, crypto corruption, & more—should be on high alert. As incoming chair of the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, I’m sending a warning to all who’ve failed to cooperate,” wrote Blumenthal on Twitter/X.

Fighting Veteran Homelessness

In advance of Veterans Day, Blumenthal, Ranking Member of the Senate Veterans Affairs Committee, joined the National Veterans Council for Legal Redress (NVCLR) and New Haven Mayor Justin Elicker to announce $1,862,000 in federal funding to build new housing for veterans.

The NVCLR Veterans Living Communities Initiative Housing Project will use the federal funding to build new permanent housing for veterans at the site of a vacant lot on Davenport Avenue. The construction will create up to five new affordable units for veterans who are coming out of transitional housing programs and potentially experiencing mental and physical health challenges or at risk of becoming homeless.

“I am so excited and honored to be here with Gary Monk of the National Veterans Council for Legal Redress, announcing almost $2 million for housing veterans. They deserve it. They served our nation. No veteran—none—should go homeless,” said Blumenthal.

Blumenthal further amplified his announcement of federal funding to build new housing for veterans on Twitter/X.

“No veteran should go homeless. Excited & honored to join the National Veterans Council for Legal Redress to announce nearly $2 million in federal funding to help create permanent housing for at-risk veterans,” wrote Blumenthal on Twitter/X.

Celebrating Revolution Wind Becoming Fully Operational

Blumenthal released a statement following the news that Revolution Wind is now fully operational.

“Today marks the beginning of a new electricity era in Connecticut. With Revolution Wind fully operational, Connecticut’s electricity supply will be greener and more affordable. With fuel costs continuing to climb, this project couldn’t have been completed at a better time. I will keep fighting to lower electricity costs and protect projects that develop clean, alternative energy sources and lessen our dependence on fossil fuels,” Blumenthal said.

Raising Alarm Over Pentagon’s Poor Treatment of Evacuated Military Families

Blumenthal, a member of the Senate Armed Services Committee, and U.S. Representatives Chris Deluzio (PA-17) and Pat Ryan (NY-18) led 30 members of Congress in a letter demanding action and answers from the Pentagon about the poor treatment of military servicemembers and their families who were evacuated from Naval Support Activity Bahrain (NSA Bahrain) in March 2026.

This letter comes after MS NOW reported on the details of a hasty and traumatic evacuation from NSA Bahrain in March, noting that many military family members have been living out of hotels and short-term rentals and are being required to pay out of pocket to cover these expenses. The letter demands that the Department of Defense right this wrong and support these evacuated military families.

The members of Congress also asked the Secretary how much it would cost to repair the severe damage to NSA Bahrain and how the incapacitation of the base has impacted U.S. operations in the Iran War and the wider Middle East.

“President Trump launched the Iran War on February 28th before evacuating the roughly 8,300 military personnel, DoD civilians, and their families stationed at NSA Bahrain. Families were authorized to evacuate only after the war started, subjecting them to the Iranian retaliatory strikes that heavily damaged the base. Since March, these evacuees have been under constant emotional, financial, and psychological stress... While the Department of Defense has provided safe haven entitlements to offset the cost of living for evacuees, this funding is scheduled to be terminated in November or after the 180th day of receiving the entitlement, before many have found permanent housing and transportation,” the letter reads.

The members continue, “Because NSA Bahrain was a critical logistics hub for U.S. Central Command, we require a better understanding of how the severe damage to the base has impacted U.S. operations… We have significant concerns about the morale and welfare of the troops deployed to the region, especially in light of the reporting on the conditions onboard the USS Gerald R. Ford and USS Abraham Lincoln, which both served record breaking deployments.”

The full text of the letter can be found here.

Blumenthal Bulletin

Blumenthal joined UAW workers striking at Triumph.

Blumenthal slammed Google for blocking schools from using Google Search unless they opt into their A.I. overview.

Blumenthal warned possible buyers of Fanendes tanker diesel that Congress is watching.

Blumenthal slammed the decision to send federal election monitors to New Haven.

title: Cassidy Delivers First Interview Following Republican Midterm Loss: “It Should Be a Lesson: Serve the American People.”
text:
WASHINGTON – U.S. Senator Bill Cassidy, M.D. (R-LA) joined The Source with Kaitlan Collins for his first interview following Tuesday’s midterm elections to discuss why he believes Republicans lost ground, what the results mean for the future of the party, and the priorities he hopes to address before leaving the Senate. Cassidy said the results should be a wake-up call for Republicans: when voters don’t believe their elected officials are addressing their concerns, they make their voices heard at the ballot box.

“If the American people perceive that a party is not serving them, that a party is asking the voter to serve their quest to keep in power, but the politician is not serving the people, the people are going to vote out the political party,” said Dr. Cassidy.

“It should just be a lesson: serve the American people, figure out what their issues are. We know health care has been expensive. We know Social Security is going insolvent. We should just make that a marquee issue,” continued Dr. Cassidy.

“It’s the opportunity for Republicans to come up with real policy solutions, not messaging bills, not entertainment on YouTube; real policy solutions that address the needs of the American people. That’s the challenge of our party. That’s what we should be doing,” said Dr. Cassidy.

title: Durbin Welcomes 26 New Citizens At Springfield’s Old State Capitol
text:
SPRINGFIELD — U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), Ranking Member of the Senate Judiciary Committee, today celebrated the naturalization of 26 new citizens from 11 countries at the Old State Capitol in Springfield. The Honorable Colleen Lawless, United States District Judge for the Central District of Illinois, and the Honorable Douglas J. Quivey, United States Magistrate Judge for the Central District of Illinois, presided over the ceremony and administered the Oath of Allegiance to the new citizens.

Durbin’s remarks as prepared for delivery are below:

“To all of you who are about to take the oath of citizenship, it is an honor to be one of the first to say to you: Hello, my fellow Americans! I also want to acknowledge your family members and friends who are here to celebrate this happy day with you. I would like to thank Judge Lawless and Judge Quivey for their role presiding over this ceremony and for inviting me to join you.

“It is a unique privilege to welcome you all as new citizens here at the Old State Capitol—a building that holds a special place in our state, and our nation’s, history. It was here where Abraham Lincoln served in the Illinois General Assembly and accepted the nomination to run for Senate against Stephen A. Douglas. Upon becoming the Republican nominee, Lincoln delivered one of his most famous speeches, where he warned our nation struggling with the moral ramifications of slavery that ‘A house divided against itself cannot stand.’

“One hundred and fifty years after Lincoln’s prescient remarks, another future president came to speak at the Old State Capitol—Barack Obama. He came to this building to announce his run for presidency, he came here to continue the work that Lincoln began 150 years before him; to bring our nation closer to the vision our founders had when they wrote the Declaration of Independence. They dreamed of a nation where all men are created equal—where each and every one of them is endowed with the rights of life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. When Obama announced his candidacy, he said ‘Each and every time, a new generation has risen up and done what's needed to be done. Today we are called once more.’ As the newest citizens of the United States of America, it is now your turn to answer the call.

“The blessing of citizenship is one that comes with responsibilities. As new citizens, you now assume the same patriotic burden placed upon all our shoulders. You must defend the Constitution from all enemies, foreign and domestic, uphold our laws, contribute to your communities, and preserve the promise of America for those who will come after you.

“I have the utmost faith in this fine group of Americans, that you all will rise to that challenge, just as the millions of immigrants who have come before you have done. This mission is especially important today, as the Trump Administration relentlessly belittles and attacks the immigrants that make our nation great.

“Even naturalization ceremonies like the one we are holding today have been scaled back and delayed under this Administration, and many would-be citizens have been left in limbo. Let me be clear: these attacks have no place in America. We are a nation of immigrants—they have made us stronger, more prosperous, and more resilient. You are the newest members of that noble tradition. And we thank you for your courage, your faith in America, and for all the hard work and perseverance that has brought you here today.

“The story of America is the story of immigrants—together you will write its next chapter. You came here as citizens of 11 nations. You will leave here as citizens of one nation: the United States of America. And this nation—your nation—welcomes you gladly. Congratulations on your tremendous achievement.”

Photos of the naturalization ceremony are available here.

-30-

title: Illinois And Midwestern Farmers Are Overcharged On Crop Insurance, Say Durbin, Duckworth, Budzinski, Sorensen, Call For USDA To Recalculate And Provide Refunds
text:
As farmers face sky-high costs, the lawmakers say USDA Risk Management Agency must rebalance premium costs and refund Illinois and Midwestern farmers

SPRINGFIELD – U.S. Senate Democratic Whip Dick Durbin (D-IL), a member of the Senate Committee on Agriculture, Nutrition, and Forestry, and U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL), along with U.S. Representatives Eric Sorensen (D-IL-17) and Nikki Budzinski (D-IL-13), both members of the House Agriculture Committee, today sent a letter to the Administrator of the U.S. Department of Agriculture (USDA) Risk Management Agency, calling for a review of the Federal Crop Insurance Program to rebalance payments for farmers that are routinely overcharged for federal crop insurance premiums. While the Federal Crop Insurance Act requires crop insurance premiums to roughly equal the indemnity payouts over the long term, Illinois corn and soybean farmers have been systemically overcharged for crop insurance premiums as they rank among the lowest in the nation for crop insurance payouts.

“Farmers face record costs for farm inputs, including diesel, fertilizer, seed, and equipment. As policymakers explore options for relief, we ask USDA to begin a targeted review as soon as possible of the counties and crops that have consistently been overcharged in the Federal Crop Insurance Program, and to accordingly reduce those crop insurance premiums,” the lawmakers wrote. “We also request that once an adjustment has been made, that USDA consider refunds to those farmers for the current crop year, and make the full correction at once to avoid prolonging this overcharging.”

As the lawmakers note, Illinois and Midwestern corn and soybean farmers have been overcharged by the Federal Crop Insurance Program as their long-term loss ratios are far below the target 1.0 loss ratio for the program. This has been documented by the University of Illinois in analyses from 2023, 2024, and two additional reports this year. New analysis from North Dakota State University (NDSU) requested by Durbin in August has shown that 10 Midwestern states, including Illinois, have long-term loss ratios far below 0.80, which means that for every dollar that Midwestern farmers have paid in premiums, less than 80 cents have gone back to them in indemnities over time. An adjustment in the Federal Crop Insurance Program to account for Midwestern farmers’ low loss ratios would provide an 11 percent decrease in premium costs for Midwestern farmers, including a 22 percent decrease for corn and a 19 percent reduction for soybeans.

The lawmakers urged USDA to immediately review the premiums rates to stop Illinois and Midwestern farmers from paying unnecessarily high costs for such a critical program.

“USDA has the authority to undertake this review and adjustment…While the USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) reviews premium rates on a rotating schedule across crops, this process has not been enough to prevent this significant overcharging of Illinois and Midwestern corn and soybean farmers,” the lawmakers wrote.

They continued: “As most farm groups have repeatedly said, crop insurance is the most important risk management tool. Farmers appreciated USDA’s decision to delay the due date for premiums this year to give farmers temporary relief. Yet, the real issue within crop insurance affordability and cash flow, is that farmers of certain crops and farmers in certain regions are being systemically overcharged.”

The lawmakers concluded their letter by underscoring that the Trump Administration’s short-sighted trade policies and war of choice in Iran have pushed farming costs sky-high, putting undue economic stress on farmers. Durbin, Duckworth, Sorensen, and Budzinski make clear that this adjustment to the Federal Crop Insurance Program would deliver critical, and deserved, relief to Midwestern farmers.

“Farmers are facing the prospect of future years of economic harm. There is a major drop in agricultural export demand due to tariffs and international conflicts. On-farm diesel costs are up by 80% over the past year, more than the on-the-road diesel prices at the pump. USDA’s own September Farm Sector Income Forecast shows that the aggregate cost of production is up $21.2 billion to nearly $493 billion,” the lawmakers wrote.

“We urge you to help farmers confronting this affordability crisis by addressing this long-standing issue of better aligning crop insurance premiums with risk, which would have the effect of cutting premium costs for thousands of farmers,” the lawmakers concluded their letter.

A copy of the letter can be found here and below:

November 6, 2026

Dear Administrator Swanson:

Farmers face record costs for farm inputs, including diesel, fertilizer, seed, and equipment. As policymakers explore options for relief, we ask USDA to begin a targeted review as soon as possible of the counties and crops that have consistently been overcharged in the Federal Crop Insurance Program, and to accordingly reduce those crop insurance premiums. We also request that once an adjustment has been made, that USDA consider refunds to those farmers for the current crop year, and make the full correction at once to avoid prolonging this overcharging.

USDA is required by law to target a 1.0 loss ratio for federal crop insurance, which means total insurance premiums should roughly equal indemnity payouts over the long-term. Unfortunately, this has not been the case for Illinois and Midwestern corn and soybean farmers, who are systematically overcharged for crop insurance premiums and have been for years. This has been substantially documented by several economic reports by the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign. Another recent analysis from North Dakota State University (NDSU) again shows that 10 Midwestern states have long-term loss ratios far below 0.80, which means that for every dollar that Midwestern farmers paid in premiums, less than 80 cents has gone back to them in indemnities over time. An NDSU simulation to bring these extremely low loss ratios closer to 0.80—still below the target of 1.0—and starting with the lowest counties first, would cut what farmers are being overcharged by $762 million per year, including more than $10 million in each of the 12 Midwestern states. A USDA adjustment of this nature would provide an 11% decrease in premium costs for Midwestern farmers, including a 22% decrease for corn and a 19% reduction for soybeans.

USDA has the authority to undertake this review and adjustment. Section 508(i) of the Federal Crop Insurance Act directs the Federal Crop Insurance Corporation to periodically review its rating methodologies, analyze rating and loss history by area, and adjust premium rates it determines are excessive for an agricultural commodity in an area. While the USDA Risk Management Agency (RMA) reviews premium rates on a rotating schedule across crops, this process has not been enough to prevent this significant overcharging of Illinois and Midwestern corn and soybean farmers.

As most farm groups have repeatedly said, crop insurance is the most important risk management tool. Farmers appreciated USDA’s decision to delay the due date for premiums this year to give farmers temporary relief. Yet, the real issue within crop insurance affordability and cash flow, is that farmers of certain crops and farmers in certain regions are being systematically overcharged.

Farmers are facing the prospect of future years of economic harm. There is a major drop in agricultural export demand due to tariffs and international conflicts. On-farm diesel costs are up by 80% over the past year, more than the on-the-road diesel prices at the pump. USDA’s own September Farm Sector Income Forecast shows that the aggregate cost of production is up $21.2 billion to nearly $493 billion. Analysis by the American Farm Bureau Federation found, despite increased prices for some commodities, that farmers are expected to operate below breakeven and could potentially be underwater into the 2027 crop year as the disruptions continue.

We urge you to help farmers confronting this affordability crisis by addressing this long-standing issue of better aligning crop insurance premiums with risk, which would have the effect of cutting premium costs for thousands of farmers. Thank you for your consideration of this request.

-30-

title: Fetterman Tours City of Washington’s Flood Prone Areas
text:
WASHINGTON, PA – Today, U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) visited the City of Washington to tour flood prone areas due to the Chartiers Creek and met with JoJo Burgess, Mayor of Washington, Demond Nixon, Mayor of East Washington, and other city officials. The group discussed further action and how the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ resource opportunities can help the City.

“I’m proud to stand by the City of Washington and the Borough of East Washington so that we can find solutions to address the flooding from Chartiers Creek. We need to use every lever of the federal government to protect people and property as flooding continues to impact the area,” said Senator Fetterman. “I applaud this joint effort and look forward to working together to turn the conclusions of this study into a reality on the ground.”

The City of Washington has dealt with flooding from the Chartiers Creek for decades and each year becoming more drastic. The US Army Corps of Engineers flood study will focus on the entirety of the Chartiers Creek watershed which runs through Washington and Allegheny Counties to the Ohio River. The study is 100% federally funded and is expected to be completed in 2028, with additional project funding to be approved by Congress. Senator Fetterman has identified resources for the City of Washington, including funding from the Army Corps and FEMA.

title: Fetterman Tours Erie Air Traffic Control Tower
text:
ERIE, PA – Today, U.S. Senator John Fetterman (D-PA) met with union representatives from the National Air Traffic Controllers Association (NATCA) and leaders at the Erie International Airport’s Air Traffic Control Tower to discuss tower operations, staffing and training, controller pay, working conditions, and upcoming technology and infrastructure improvements at Erie International Airport.

“Air traffic controllers have high pressure jobs with absolutely zero room for error. We need to recognize the importance of their work by investing in our airspace and giving them the resources and support they need,” said Senator Fetterman. “I’m deeply grateful for the opportunity to hear from our air traffic controllers and union members at Erie Tower and learn more about all they do to keep Northwestern Pennsylvania’s skies safe.”

NATCA is the primary labor union representing 20,000 aviation safety professionals, including air traffic controllers, nationwide. The organization advocates for aviation safety, adequate staffing, workforce protections, and national modernization of air traffic control infrastructure.

As a member of the Senate Commerce Committee’s Subcommittee on Aviation, Space, and Innovation, Senator Fetterman is committed to aviation safety. During the 119th Congress, he joined his colleagues in unanimously passing the ROTOR Act to strengthen aviation safety technology standards. In September, he also joined his colleagues in passing U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth’s (D-IL) Aviation Medication Transparency Act and U.S. Senator John Hoeven’s (R-ND) John A. Hauser Mental Health in Aviation Act to improve Federal Aviation Administration medication guidelines and mental health access for air traffic controllers, respectively.

title: Gallego joins TMZ, Grills Elon Musk and Calls on Him to Testify
text:

title: Gillibrand, Schumer Announce Nearly $2 Million In USDA Funding For New York State
text:

title: Q&A: Unfinished Business
text:
With U.S. Senator Chuck Grassley

Q: What’s on Congress’ plate before the end of the year?

A: With the midterm elections behind us, the 119th Congress returns to Washington with a plate of unfinished business to address. That includes passing the annual defense authorization bill, keeping the government open beyond the short-term funding bill that expires on Dec. 11 and reauthorizing key rural healthcare programs, including the Medicare-dependent and low-volume hospital programs, Rural Community Hospital Demonstration Program and a Medicare payment floor for rural doctors and clinics. For 65 years in a row, Congress has worked across the aisle to pass the National Defense Authorization Act (NDAA). The annual legislation sets defense-related policy and authorizes appropriations for the Pentagon, such as procurement for weapon systems, ships, and aircraft; payroll and personnel; military construction; and, nuclear weapons programs at the Department of Energy. The NDAA is often called must-pass legislation because it authorizes funding that supports military families, from housing to healthcare, and sets guidance on the nation’s defense programs that protect national security. It’s one of the most consequential bills every year on Congress’ to do list. For example, the fiscal year 2025 NDAA included 794 pages of policy measures and discretionary authorizations exceeding $883 billion. The bill is often a vehicle for other homeland security legislation to get passed. This year, I’ve filed bipartisan amendments to the NDAA that would protect kids online, fight organized crime and stem illicit drug use.

I’ll also be pushing to enact the five-year Farm Bill that’s been stalled for the last three years and operating under annual extensions. Unfortunately, Senate Democrats have refused to join Republican-led efforts to cut fraud from the food stamp program. Meanwhile, farmers need certainty and are counting on Congress to update conservation, rural development and farm credit policies that are operating under the 2018 farm law. I’m also committed to getting permanent, year-round nationwide E15 across the finish line that was included in the Farm Bill that passed the Senate Agriculture Committee. Getting E15 signed into law will help lower gas prices, boost corn demand and pump $14 billion into the farm economy. I’m hopeful lawmakers will reach a consensus once and for all to get the Farm Bill to the president’s desk before the end of the year.

Q: Why is permitting reform a bipartisan priority?

A: There is too much red tape in Washington. Public policies set decades ago to protect the environment are in dire need of an update to reflect changes in technology and address the regulatory and legal quagmire that’s standing in the way of bringing costs down for the American people. The federal permitting process that determines when and if critical infrastructure projects move from the drawing board to shovels in the ground is ineffective and costly. The heavy-handed bureaucratic review process is forcing American families to pay more for energy and consumer goods. Lawmakers on the Senate Environment and Public Works Committee and the Energy and Natural Resources Committee have rolled up their sleeves in good faith to hammer out a bipartisan bill called the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act. It would reform the nation’s environmental review and federal permitting framework that’s driving up costs for Americans and impeding economic growth. By responsibly untangling the regulatory thicket that takes years and even decades for infrastructure projects to get started — from pipelines to transmission lines needed to boost the nation’s energy grid — Congress can fix the broken permitting process, better protect natural resources, pave the way for more affordable and reliable clean energy and foster economic development across the country. Importantly, the bill would help provide certainty to infrastructure projects that have received permitting approvals and secured financing by preventing future administrations from unwinding or blocking entire classes of energy projects. What’s more, the Senate bill would ensure data centers pay for their energy costs and protect families from footing the bill. For years, Congress has taken bites at the permitting reform apple. It’s time to get the job done and responsibly meet surging demand for affordable electricity so the U.S. economy isn’t left behind.

title: Heinrich Demands Answers on Trump Administration’s Push to Build Data Centers on Public Lands
text:
Heinrich: “I am extremely concerned with the Trump administration's actions to develop data centers on public lands.”

WASHINGTON — Today, U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee, raised the alarm on the Trump administration’s push to develop AI data centers on public lands, demanding answers from Bureau of Land Management (BLM) Director Steve Pearce on the agency’s actions to greenlight data center buildout.

“I am extremely concerned with the Trump administration’s actions to develop data centers on public lands,” Heinrich began.

Heinrich’s letter follows his online post earlier today stating simply, “No data centers on public lands. Period.”

Heinrich's letter to Pearce comes after multiple actions from the Trump administration to develop data centers on public lands, including the June 2026 BLM approval of the 88-acre Townsite Data Center in Boulder City, Nevada. While the project was paused by the Department of the Interior’s Board of Land Appeals in September 2026, its approval was initially spurred by a 2025 Trump Executive Order that expedited the permitting of data center development on public lands.

BLM is now reportedly considering at least 15 proposals to build data centers or related infrastructure on public lands, covering more than 17,000 acres of public lands and stretching across six Western states. According to the Salt Lake Tribune, BLM asked state directors to identify public lands ready for data center development — something the Department of the Interior’s leadership told officials is a high priority.

“When BLM makes decisions about public land, it should always consider the best interest of the public and the communities that will be directly impacted by its decision,” Heinrich wrote.

“BLM should listen to the voices of the American people and carefully consider the many uses of public land before hastily greenlighting data center buildout on public lands,” Heinrich continued.

In the letter, Heinrich specifically requests a complete list of all authorities BLM is using to support data center development on public lands, all data center-related development proposals BLM is considering on public lands, and the public lands BLM has identified that are eligible for data center development.

Read the full letter here and below.

Director Pearce:

I am extremely concerned with the Trump administration’s actions to develop data centers on public lands.

In June 2026, the Bureau of Land Management (BLM) approved the first data center on public lands—the sprawling 88-acre Townsite Data Center located in Boulder City, Nevada. At the time, BLM amended an existing right-of-way grant for a solar and battery-storage project to allow for the development of the data center. On September 1, following an appeal by Boulder City, Nevada, and environmental groups, the Department of the Interior’s Board of Land Appeals paused development of the data center, citing BLM’s decision to approve the project without conducting a new National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) review. The Board found that Boulder City and the environmental groups “made a persuasive showing that BLM violated NEPA and acted arbitrarily or capriciously when it determined that the data center project is ‘substantially the same’ as the solar plant project for purposes of its NEPA analysis.”

BLM’s decision to approve the Townsite Data Center followed an Executive Order signed by President Trump in July 2025 that expedited the permitting of data centers on public lands. In September, the President signed another Executive Order that grants Secretary Burgum additional independent authorities over energy production on public lands. BLM is now reportedly considering at least 15 proposals to build data centers or related infrastructure on public lands. The development proposals cover more than 17,000 acres of public lands and stretch across six western states. According to a report, BLM recently asked state directors to identify public lands ready for data center development and the Department of the Interior’s leadership told officials that the topic is high priority.

When BLM makes decisions about public land, it should always consider the best interest of the public and the communities that will be directly impacted by its decision. The Multiple Use – Sustained Yield principle of public land management requires the BLM to consider the other uses of public land when considering whether to site a data center in any specific location. BLM should listen to the voices of the American people and carefully consider the many uses of public land before hastily greenlighting data center buildout on public lands.

In light of questions and concerns about BLM’s review of data center development proposals on public lands and related actions, I request you provide the following information by November 20, 2026:

A complete list of all authorities BLM is using to support data center development on public lands. Please include the specific precedent and legal rationale.

A complete list of all data center related development proposals BLM is considering on public lands. For each proposal, please include the specific entity that is backing the project; the precise location of the project; the total acreage of federally owned land under review for development; the precise use of the federally owned land under review for development (e.g., for transmission lines, roads, or physical data center structures); whether the review will entail a NEPA review, or in the case of an existing right-of-way grant, a new NEPA review; and whether the proposal will have a public comment period.

A complete list of all public lands BLM has identified that are eligible for data center development.

Thank you for your prompt attention to this request. Should you have any questions, please do not hesitate to contact my staff at (202) 224-4971.

Sincerely,

title: NEW DATA: Heinrich’s Bipartisan American Affordability & Jobs Act Will Hold Data Centers Accountable, Lower Electricity Bills by $50-78 Annually, Save $54 Billion in Health-Related Costs, and Lead to Cleaner Air and Healthier Communities
text:
ALBUQUERQUE, N.M.– New independent analyses released this week from the Solar Energy Industries Association (SEIA), Rhodium Group, and Grid Strategies LLC find that Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee U.S. Senator Martin Heinrich’s (D-N.M.) Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act (BAAJA) would lower household electricity bills by $50 to $78 annually by 2040, reduce power sector emissions by approximately 20 percent, and avoid $54 billion in cumulative public health damages.

The analyses also find that the legislation would accelerate the connection of clean energy projects to the grid and require data centers to pay billions more toward the transmission infrastructure needed to serve their electricity demand.

“Americans are tired of paying more in utility bills while projects that could lower costs sit stuck in the planning phase for years,” said Heinrich. “These independent analyses show exactly what we stand to gain by fixing our broken permitting system: lower electricity bills, cleaner air, healthier communities, and more reliable energy infrastructure. BAAJA will help get more affordable energy connected to the grid while making sure massive energy consumers like data centers pay up. We should be building the infrastructure America needs, not making families foot the bill for permitting delays.”

BAAJA will deliver lower costs and cleaner air for Americans:

Lower electricity bills: Reduce household electricity bills by $50 to $78 annually by 2040, representing a 3–5 percent decrease in electricity prices, according to Rhodium Group.

Reduce pollution: Cut cumulative power sector CO2 emissions by approximately 20 percent between 2028 and 2035 compared with current law, according to SEIA.

Save billions in health costs: Reduce cumulative public health damages by an estimated $54 billion, according to SEIA.

Accelerate clean energy: Enable an additional 167 Gigawatt Alternating Current (GWac) of net solar capacity additions between 2028 and 2035 compared with current law, according to SEIA.

Connect more clean energy to the grid: Drive an additional 17–249 Gigawatts (GW) of clean energy resources to connect to the grid through 2040, according to Rhodium Group.

Increase clean energy generation: Increase solar and wind generation to 37.4 percent of total power generation, compared with 19.6 percent under the current permitting regime, according to SEIA.

Avoid massive amounts of emissions: Avoid as much as 1.5 gigatons of cumulative emissions through 2040, according to Rhodium Group — equivalent to almost 35 million gasoline-powered cars off the road or taking 39 coal plants offline for a decade.

BAAJA will also make data centers pay their fair share:

Recover $55 billion in transmission costs: Grid Strategies estimates that changes to federal transmission pricing policy under BAAJA could result in data centers contributing approximately $55 billion toward transmission costs over the next decade.

Collect $35 billion more from data centers: That represents approximately $35 billion more than data centers would otherwise pay under current policy.

title: Sen. Markey, Rep. Adams Reintroduce Legislation to Protect Critical Records from Environmental Damage
text:
Bill Text (PDF)

Washington (November 6, 2026) - Senator Edward J. Markey (D-Mass.), a member of the Health, Education, Labor and Pensions (HELP) Committee and Environment and Public Works Committee, and Congresswoman Alma Adams, Ph.D. (NC-12) today announced the introduction of the Public Archives Resiliency Act to authorize grants to support long-term climate resiliency, preservation, and continuity of records and documents for archival intuitions, including libraries and museums.

As the climate crisis continues to worsen, the need to protect historic government records from damage is vital. This includes records generated through birth, death, marriage, taxes, military service, education, immigration, property ownership and much more. Too many of the institutions responsible for managing the preservation of these documents are at risk of environmental damage and lack the necessary resources to protect the indispensable records of their communities. If these records are destroyed, individuals’ ability to access critical government benefits and services are delayed and historic cultural artifacts are lost.

“Our nation’s history is not only told through monuments, museums, and founding documents—it’s written in birth certificates, marriage licenses, military records, and countless other documents that tell the stories of everyday Americans,” said Senator Markey. “As we celebrate America’s 250th birthday, we must ensure that Americans’ irreplaceable personal records are protected from environmental catastrophe. The Public Archives Resiliency Act will help safeguard these vital records from climate-fueled disasters, protecting Americans’ identities, rights, and benefits for years to come.”

“I am proud to reintroduce the Public Archives Resiliency Act with Senator Markey,” said Congresswoman Adams. “Protecting public registries, Tribal records, museums, and libraries is an essential part of preserving our nation’s cultural identity. This bill will ensure that our record-keeping institutions have the resources to withstand future disastrous events, so that no family will lose the documents safeguarding their legal and financial rights.”

“America’s archives have a unique role in underpinning legal and civic life, and preserving cultural memory. Archives are part of the foundational infrastructure of our democracy. The growing frequency and severity of climate change-related disasters have serious consequences for America’s archives and the archivists who steward these vital records. This legislation is critically important to address this increasingly urgent issue, and to safeguard our shared American history,” said Eira Tansey, internationally recognized expert on the impacts of climate change on archives, and author of A Green New Deal for Archives.

“For over forty years, America’s repositories have been trapped in what an early 1980s National Historical Publications & Records Commission (NHPRC) report termed ‘a cycle of poverty’—bearing the weight of structural underfunding and precarious staffing while stewarding the bedrock of our nation’s civic memory. Chronic underfunding directly compounds this crisis: it leaves facilities vulnerable to severe weather, stalls preventative mitigation, and denies staff the capacity to build emergency safeguards before disaster strikes. The Public Archives Resiliency Act is the vital federal intervention we have needed for decades. By investing directly in archival workers and resilient infrastructure through the Institute of Museum and Library Services (IMLS) and NHPRC, this legislation breaks that exhausting cycle and ensures our democracy’s documentary heritage will endure,” said Brenda Gunn, President of the Society of American Archivists.

“The resiliency of our public archives is a cornerstone of democratic accountability and constitutional governance. Budget pressures, uncertain grant funding, and other challenges across the United States underscore the need for increased public support for independent, secure archives. Individuals often rely on the creation and preservation of records - censuses, taxes, military service, education, legal proceedings, property ownership, among others - to protect their rights and property, to secure benefits, and to recover from disaster. We must invest in the institutions and people that accomplish this essential work to be sure these records are collected, preserved, and made accessible without disruption,” said Joy Banks, Executive Director of the Council of State Archivists.

###

title: Sen. Moran Hosts Under Secretary of War Michael Duffey in Wichita
text:
WICHITA, Kan. – U.S. Senator Jerry Moran (R-Kan.) – a senior member of the Senate Appropriations Subcommittee on Defense – today hosted Michael P. Duffey, the Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment, in Kansas to tour the defense manufacturing capabilities at the National Institute for Aviation Research (NIAR) at Wichita State University (WSU). The tour highlighted NIAR’s advanced engineering and manufacturing capabilities that are helping address defense sustainment challenges across the department by keeping aging military aircraft, including the B-1 bomber, operational and mission-ready.

“Thank you to Under Secretary Duffey for accepting my invitation to visit Kansas and see firsthand the talent, expertise and advanced defense manufacturing capabilities we have here in Wichita,” said Sen. Moran. “NIAR’s work is helping address sustainment challenges, improve military readiness and support the men and women of our armed forces. As a senior defense appropriator, I will continue working to strengthen our national defense and support the critical partnerships that are providing America’s servicemembers with the resources and tools necessary to protect our nation.”

“It’s great to be in Wichita today with Senator Moran. He is a steadfast champion for the warfighter, the people of Kansas, and the work of the National Institute for Aviation Research at Wichita State University,” said Under Secretary of War for Acquisition and Sustainment Michael P. Duffey. “His leadership in the Senate and advocacy for Kansas are strengthening the industrial base, advancing innovation, and delivering the readiness our military needs to fight and win.”

“It was an honor and privilege to show Under Secretary Duffey how the talent, innovation and technology at Wichita State is being leveraged to save time, money and resources in order to reinforce the strength of U.S. military fleets,” said John Tomblin, WSU Executive Vice President for Research and Industry & Defense Programs and NIAR Executive Director. “We will continue to work with our partners to develop solutions to the nation’s most challenging aerospace and defense challenges.”
