title: Murphy Statement on Discharge from Hospital
text:
WASHINGTON, DC — U.S. Senator Chris Murphy (D-Conn.) released the following statement upon discharge from The Johns Hopkins Hospital. Murphy will miss the next several weeks of votes in the Senate as he continues his recovery.

“Thank you for the outpouring of support my family and I have received over the last few days. I want to be direct with you, so here is my diagnosis. Last Saturday afternoon, I felt something was not right with my body and called 9-1-1 out of an abundance of caution, and I’m glad I did. I was diagnosed with a small bleed in the thalamus region of my brain.

“The doctors are very encouraged by the progress I’ve made so far. In order to take my recovery seriously and get back to work on the quickest timeline possible, I will be spending several weeks at a rehabilitation center after being discharged from the hospital today.

“This has been a scary experience for me and my family, and I appreciate the continued respect for our privacy. As I'm working towards a full recovery, I am staying engaged with my team and colleagues remotely, and my staff continues to carry out our legislative priorities, serve constituents, and ensure the work of my office continues uninterrupted. I want to extend my deepest thanks to the excellent doctors and staff at Johns Hopkins who have treated me and cared for my family.”

Statement from Dr. Jose Suarez, Chief of Neurosciences Critical Care at The Johns Hopkins Hospital:

“Senator Murphy experienced a small hemorrhagic stroke. He has shown tremendous progress, and at the current rate of improvement, we expect that he will make a full recovery following rehabilitation.”

title: ON THE JOB FOR MICHIGAN: Hemlock Semiconductor CEO Highlights Peters’ Efforts to Expand U.S. Semiconductor Production, Support Michigan Industries and Workers
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – In a new “On the Job” video from U.S. Senator Gary Peters’ (MI) office, Hemlock Semiconductor (HSC) Chairman and CEO AB Ghosh highlights Peters’ efforts to expand U.S. production of semiconductor chips, which are critical to Michigan’s auto industry and products ranging from cars, cell phones, home appliances, solar panels, agriculture equipment, and defense technologies. HSC, headquartered in Hemlock, Michigan, is the nation’s leading producer of hyper-pure polysilicon for the semiconductor industry and one of only five companies in the world capable of producing the highest quality polysilicon for semiconductor chips. Peters helped pass the CHIPS and Science Act into law, including a provision Peters authored that ensures federal incentives to boost semiconductor manufacturing include U.S. suppliers that produce the materials for semiconductor manufacturing, such as HSC. This provision ensured HSC would be eligible for the $325 million in federal funding it was awarded in 2024 to build a new, state-of-the-art manufacturing facility on its existing campus in Hemlock, creating thousands of good-paying jobs in Michigan. The video is part of the On the Job for Michigan series, which highlights Peters’ leadership and advocacy on behalf of Michigan constituents and communities.

“[Hemlock Semiconductor] serves two critical supply chains, namely semiconductors and solar energy, which is critical for U.S. national security and its energy independence,” said HSC Chairman and CEO AB Ghosh. “The CHIPS and Science Act was the first big legislation put down to onshore the tech supply chain. This grant of $325 million is critical for the future generation of this business. It’s going to allow us to make the polysilicon for the next generation AI chips, and that’s critical for the U.S. nation.”

“The work that we're doing here, it's awesome because there's only a handful of companies that can even produce the material at this purity level,” said Strategic Project Leader Elizabeth Stelzer. “And so, we get to play a part in making sure that the supply chain is steady and stable.”

Watch the “On The Job” video here.

“Semiconductor chips are critical to both U.S. national security and the future of our auto industry here in Michigan,” said Peters. “I believe you can't be a great country unless you actually make things, and they’re making great things right here at Hemlock Semiconductor. We must continue to support their cutting-edge work to strengthen this essential supply chain and create good-paying, local jobs.”

Peters has made strengthening American manufacturing and securing domestic supply chains a top priority. The CHIPS and Science Act also includes a provision Peters authored to support the domestic production of mature semiconductor technologies and ensure that projects supporting critical manufacturing industries are given priority status, which would include the automotive sector. This was in addition to $50 billion already in the law to incentivize U.S. production of all types of semiconductors, for a total of $52 billion. The CHIPS and Science Act additionally authorized increased funding for the Manufacturing Extension Partnership (MEP) program, which has been a priority for Peters.

Last year, the Senate passed Peters’ bipartisan legislation to strengthen federal efforts to expand domestic manufacturing of semiconductor chips. Peters’ Securing Semiconductor Supply Chains Act would direct the U.S. Department of Commerce’s SelectUSA program, in collaboration with other federal agencies and state economic development organizations, to develop strategies that would attract investment in U.S. semiconductor manufacturers and supply chains. The Senate also passed Peters’ bipartisan legislation to establish a National Manufacturing Advisory Council at the U.S. Department of Commerce to help strengthen federal manufacturing policy and U.S. leadership in global manufacturing.

Peters also helped enact the Bipartisan Infrastructure Law, which includes a provision authored by Peters to strengthen Buy American requirements and close loopholes to ensure the federal government is spending taxpayer dollars on American-made products that support American companies and workers. Peters additionally supported and helped pass the Inflation Reduction Act to strengthen domestic manufacturing of clean energy technologies and create millions of American jobs.

###

title: Ahead of Veterans Day, Rosen, Blackburn Announce Introduction of Bipartisan Bills to Support Veteran Education Programs
text:
WASHINGTON, DC – Ahead of Veterans Day, U.S. Senators Jacky Rosen (D-NV) and Marsha Blackburn (R-TN) announced the introduction of two bipartisan bills to support and improve veterans’ education and career programs. The first bill, the Veterans Education Empowerment Act, would reauthorize and improve a grant program that helps establish and fund student veterans centers at colleges and universities. These centers serve as a critical resource for nearly one million veterans attending college each year, ensuring they have the support they need as they transition to the classroom and workforce.

The Senators also introduced the Veteran Technology Employment Success Act, a bill to improve the VET TEC High Technology program, which funds short-term, high-tech training for veterans and servicemembers to start careers in the tech industry. Specifically, this bill would require the VA to collect data on the success of the program and update implementation to ensure the training veterans receive is in line with industry demands.

“We owe our servicemembers an immense debt of gratitude for the sacrifices they have made, and the least we can do is to make sure they have the support and resources they need as they transition back to civilian life,” said Senator Rosen. “I’m proud to introduce these bipartisan bills to make pursuing an education or a technical career a little bit easier, allowing them to learn critical skills needed to succeed in today’s world.”

“Our veterans have earned every opportunity to succeed after their service, and the Veterans Education Empowerment Act will reauthorize and strengthen the student veteran centers that support nearly one million of them as they navigate higher education and pursue career opportunities,” said Senator Blackburn. “At the same time, the Veteran Technology Employment Success Act will improve the VET TEC program by requiring the VA to track results and align high-tech training with real industry demands.”

Senator Rosen has been a champion for Nevada’s veterans and their families. She recently helped introduce legislation to improve coordination between the VA and state veterans’ agencies to better connect veterans with their benefits. In September, Senator Rosen also introduced a bipartisan bill to improve veterans’ access to medical care in rural areas. Additionally, Senator Rosen is leading the charge in Congress to require the Department of Defense to join the Department of Energy in identifying all servicemembers and veterans who worked at locations where radiation and toxic exposure occurred, such as the Nevada Test and Training Range, and provide them with the same presumption of exposure, allowing such veterans to better access the VA health care and benefits they have earned. Last year, Senator Rosen introduced bipartisan legislation to incentivize employers to hire student veterans for part-time work and paid internships.

title: NEWS: After EPA Proposes Plan to Remove Federal Protections for Wetlands and Streams, Sens. Schiff, Markey Push EPA to Abandon Extreme Threat to Clean Drinking Water
text:
Senators write: “…The definitions proposed by the SNPRM [Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking] would remove federal protections for 80 percent of streams in the United States and 95 percent of individual wetlands, which makes a mockery of the congressional intent behind the Clean Water Act.”

Washington, D.C. – U.S. Senators Adam Schiff (D-Calif.), Ranking Member of the Senate Environment and Public Works’ Fisheries, Water, and Wildlife Subcommittee, and Ed Markey (D-Mass.) are calling on the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers (USACE) to abandon their new proposal that threatens to harm public health and leave communities vulnerable to flooding and loss of access to clean drinking water.

The EPA’s new proposal to revise the definition of the Waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule replaces the proposed November 2025 standard with an even more extreme one, defining “relatively permanent” to mean “perennial” waters, stripping federal protections for hundreds of bodies of waters. Previously, in January 2026, the Senators urged the agencies to reverse this proposal.

“As we explained then, excluding these waters from federal protection threatens drinking water, increases downstream pollution and flood risk, and shifts substantial costs onto states, communities, and ratepayers. We are disappointed that your agencies have not only chosen to disregard all of these concerns, but have put out a second, more extreme proposal that does even more harm. We urge you to abandon this effort altogether and remember your statutory responsibilities to protect drinking water, public health, and the environment,” the Senators wrote in a letter to the EPA.

EPA’s latest proposal goes further to eliminate safeguards on bodies of waters that were already reduced by the Supreme Court’s 2023 decision in Sackett v. EPA. Additionally, the Senators raise concern with the subsequent harms this proposal will have on state and tribes’ capacity to manage waters, as well as on American households, who will bear the financial costs.

“…Pollution does not respect the arbitrary boundaries laid out in these proposals. When upstream waters lose federal protection, downstream communities do not cease experiencing their effects of that loss…the costs of additional pollution, degraded drinking water sources and the associated health risks, diminished flood protection, and lost aquatic habitat are shifted to states, Tribes, municipalities, water utilities, and ultimately the American taxpayer,” the Senators wrote.

“The Clean Water Act was enacted to “restore and maintain the chemical, physical, and biological integrity of the Nation’s waters.” Proposing to systematically exclude waters known to be critical to that integrity ignores science and defeats the purpose of the Act…We urge you to abandon this disastrous SNPRM as well as the 2025 proposal and leave the 2023 conforming rule in place,” the Senators concluded.

The EPW Committee’s Ranking Member, U.S. Senator Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), also signed the letter.

The full text of the letter can be found here and below.

Dear Administrator Zeldin and Mr. Forsgren:

We write to express our serious concern regarding the U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA) and U.S. Army Corps of Engineers’ September 9, 2026 Supplemental Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (SNPRM) that proposes to further narrow which waters would receive federal protections under the Clean Water Act. On January 28, 2026, we urged the agencies to abandon the proposed 2025 waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule. As we explained then, excluding these waters from federal protection threatens drinking water, increases downstream pollution and flood risk, and shifts substantial costs onto states, communities, and ratepayers. We are disappointed that your agencies have not only chosen to disregard all of these concerns, but have put out a second, more extreme proposal that does even more harm. We urge you to abandon this effort altogether and remember your statutory responsibilities to protect drinking water, public health, and the environment.

The core proposal of the SNPRM is to define “relatively permanent” waters to include only perennial waters, which the proposal suggests defining as “having standing or continuously flowing water every day of the year during ordinary conditions.” The SNPRM includes limited exceptions for drought, dry spells, and low tides, and allows only a single interruption of no more than 30 consecutive days annually. The SNPRM also considers a definition of “continuous surface connection” that would require even perennial surface water within a wetland to be continuously connected to a jurisdictional water in order to merit protection as WOTUS.

Limiting “relatively permanent” waters to perennial and interconnected waters would be scientifically indefensible and would put downstream water quality at risk. EPA’s own scientific record demonstrates why. EPA’s review of more than 1,200 peer-reviewed studies concluded that streams are connected to downstream waters regardless of their size or frequency of flow and strongly influence downstream physical, chemical, and biological conditions. That review, and numerous other independent scientific studies, found that perennial, intermittent, and ephemeral tributaries transport water, sediment, nutrients, contaminants, organic material, and organisms through river networks and collectively affect larger downstream waters. Further, the definitions proposed by the SNPRM would remove federal protections for 80 percent of streams in the United States and 95 percent of individual wetlands, which makes a mockery of the congressional intent behind the Clean Water Act.

Your agencies acknowledge these concerns in the SNPRM and recognize the functions served by ephemeral streams. The agencies also acknowledge that the majority of wetlands would not satisfy the supplemental definition of “continuous surface connection,” because most wetlands do not contain perennial surface water. Even more, your agencies concede that the 30-day threshold is not “scientifically-grounded” and is proposed only because it is “easy to administer.” Given these acknowledgements, it appears the entirety of the SNPRM is contradictory— proposing changes that go against the very scientific findings cited in the notice. “Easy to administer” does not justify the neglect of waterways that contribute on average 55% of the water found in larger rivers – the protection of which is the mission of your agencies and the Clean Water Act.

The SNPRM also includes an arbitrary five-year cutoff for waters impacted by drought conditions, a policy that would cause particular harm to more arid regions like the West. After five years of dry conditions, such drought conditions would be treated as the new baseline. As American Rivers explains in its public comment, this would “convert a growing share of currently ‘relatively permanent’ waters to non-jurisdictional status over time, particularly in the West, as droughts lengthen and recur more frequently.”

The agencies justify these contradictions and known harms in part by claiming that the proposal allegedly provides regulatory clarity, giving landowners clearer notice of Clean Water Act obligations. But administrative simplicity cannot provide cover for a scientifically and legally indefensible interpretation of the Clean Water Act, as its primary purpose is to protect waters from pollution. Moreover, this SNPRM would not provide clarity, as it would inevitably lead to litigation and overwhelm state and tribal capacity to manage waters. The agencies acknowledge in the supplemental proposal that “Tribes may disproportionately rely on the Federal Government for water program implementation and enforcement of water quality violations” and “many Tribes are still building capacity and may lack resources to create a Tribal water program.” This SNPRM will remove federal protections for many waters Tribes may care about, thus pulling the rug out from under them.

As we emphasized in January, pollution does not respect the arbitrary boundaries laid out in these proposals. When upstream waters lose federal protection, downstream communities do not cease experiencing their effects of that loss. And states are not going to be able to fill the gaps left by the SNPRM. One state’s hypothetical capacity to regulate their own waters, absent federal law, does not mean as much when an under-resourced, upstream state exports the cost of their water quality remediation downstream. Instead, the costs of additional pollution, degraded drinking water sources and the associated health risks, diminished flood protection, and lost aquatic habitat are shifted to states, Tribes, municipalities, water utilities, and ultimately the American taxpayer. Our previous letter warned that narrowing WOTUS in this manner would transfer responsibility and costs downstream rather than eliminate them. The recent supplemental proposal fails to heed that warning and would multiply these costs to the American people.

The Clean Water Act was enacted to “restore and maintain the chemical, physical, and biological integrity of the Nation’s waters.” Proposing to systematically exclude waters known to be critical to that integrity ignores science and defeats the purpose of the Act. Although we do not agree with its reasoning, the Supreme Court spoke in Sackett v. EPA, and EPA and the Corps conformed to that decision in 2023. There is no need for a further rulemaking, especially when that rulemaking envisions slashing federal water protections even further than the Supreme Court already has. The SNPRM your agencies have published includes a litany of contradictions and acknowledged significant harm to human health and the environment. We urge you to abandon this disastrous SNPRM as well as the 2025 proposal and leave the 2023 conforming rule in place.

title: Sen. Tim Scott gathers Charleston leaders for housing roundtable
text:
NORTH CHARLESTON, S.C. — Inside the council chambers at North Charleston City Hall, U.S. Senator Tim Scott (R-S.C.) brought together mayors, state legislators, county leaders, builders and business leaders from across the Lowcountry on Friday to put his 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act to work in South Carolina.

“Your efforts will allow the ROAD to Housing Act to hit the ground running throughout South Carolina,” said Sen. Scott. “One of the biggest motivating factors for my work on housing is remembering how I grew up in a single-parent household, mired in poverty, sharing a bedroom and a bed with my mom and my brother in a rental unit with dirt for the front yard and no backyard. The better we make people’s lives today, the brighter our future is together here at home in the great state of South Carolina.”

Fred Moore, housing advisor to Sen. Scott, walked participants through how the law clears the way for new construction and gives local leaders more flexibility to build. Bradford Traywick, regional director for Sen. Scott, led the conversation, which turned quickly to the Lowcountry’s biggest pressure points: workforce housing near new jobs, permitting timelines and zoning that keeps starter homes off the market.

“I want to thank Senator Scott and his staff for doing this. The information that was shared is so important, especially for folks from local government who are on the ground and actually doing the work. We have a major housing need: affordable housing, workforce housing, even market-rate housing and student housing in Orangeburg,” said Sidney Evering II, city administrator for the City of Orangeburg.

“Thanks to the Senator and the Banking Committee, what we have now is something that can really make a difference, to make that process more efficient, actually more business-like. My peers all across the country are talking about this act and trying to understand it. To be able to go to a forum here, in our community, and have someone from the staff come and explain it to us, that’s incredibly valuable,” said Kevin Sheilley, president and CEO of the Charleston Metro Chamber of Commerce.

“Housing is the crux of the entire conversation for economic development, for growth, for job opportunities. It’s a conversation we have all day long in our office when it comes to our employees being able to afford to live where they work. The growth here is not stopping, so we need to lean in,” said Marie Delcioppo, executive director of marketing and business development at Stubbs Muldrow Herin Architects.

“From what I understand, the ROAD to Housing Act is one of the most significant pieces of legislation in decades, and I’m excited to see what it can do for families across South Carolina. Dorchester County is growing fast, and I think this legislation will help us make sure we have the workforce for all of the great companies in the tri-county region,” said Gordon Rooney of Dorchester County Economic Development.

The North Charleston roundtable closed a three-city series that included stops in Duncan on October 28 and Columbia on October 29.

Watch the full event recap video here.

Background

In July 2025, Sen. Scott led the Senate Banking Committee in unanimously advancing the ROAD to Housing Act.

In March 2026, the full Senate passed the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act by a vote of 89-10.

On July 11, 2026, the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act became law.

The law cuts red tape, unlocks housing supply and lowers costs for families, with no new federal spending.

title: ICYMI: Shaheen Receives Lifetime Achievement Award from New Hampshire Community Loan Fund for Championing Affordable Housing
text:
(Manchester, NH) – Yesterday, U.S. Senator Jeanne Shaheen (D-NH) was honored by the New Hampshire Community Loan Fund with its Community Champion Lifetime Achievement Award. The award was presented in recognition of Shaheen’s work on behalf of New Hampshire’s Resident Owned Communities (ROCs) and her efforts to expand affordable housing in the state. Shaheen also delivered remarks at the Annual Meeting, which is the New Hampshire Community Loan Fund’s marquee event. The nonprofit provides loans, coaching and guidance to New Hampshire communities and has invested more than $518 million in communities across the Granite State since its founding in 1983. Photos from the event can be found HERE.

“For over 40 years, the New Hampshire Community Loan Fund has provided transformative financial support, guidance and counseling to individuals, families and organizations across the Granite State. Nothing describes the organization’s philosophy better than ‘Neighbors Helping Neighbors,’ and its work has been indispensable to unlocking economic opportunity throughout New Hampshire,” said Senator Shaheen. “It is humbling to receive this Lifetime Achievement Award from such a critical institution in the state. I’ve been so proud to work alongside the Community Loan Fund, investors and local leaders to make great strides in advancing affordable housing, supporting manufactured housing communities and bolstering economic growth across New Hampshire.”

Throughout her time in the Senate, Shaheen has led efforts to lower housing costs, expand affordable housing and support New Hampshire’s manufactured housing communities. Earlier this year, Shaheen helped pass the landmark 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act, which, along with cutting red tape and streamlining the federal housing process, will directly lower construction costs for new, affordable manufactured housing. In the bill, Senator Shaheen secured three key provisions, which include the Preservation and Reinvestment Initiative in Community Enhancement (PRICE) Act to extend a federal grant program that provides funding to support the purchase, construction and renovation of manufactured housing communities, the Strategy and Investment in Rural Housing Preservation Act and the Streamlining Rural Housing Act.

title: U.S. Senators Tina Smith, Amy Klobuchar Secure $28.6 Million to Improve Railroad Safety, Efficiency and Reliability in Minnesota
text:
The federal grants will upgrade tracks, equipment and rail cars in Greater MN and the Twin Cities metro

WASHINGTON, D.C. – U.S. Senators Amy Klobuchar (D-MN) and Tina Smith (D-MN) secured $28.6 million in three separate U.S. Department of Transportation grants to improve railroad infrastructure, safety and reliability in Minnesota. The funds will ensure Minnesota’s railroad network can continue to safely move people, commodities and other goods that power small towns, rural communities and big cities.

“Minnesota farmers and businesses depend on a safe and reliable rail system to get their products to market and keep our economy moving. These federal grants will replace aging tracks, boost efficiency, and improve rail safety,” said Sen. Klobuchar. “Maintaining strong rail infrastructure is critical for the long-term economic well-being of our state and for keeping Minnesota competitive.”

“Railroads are the lifeblood for Minnesota farmers, producers and small businesses,” said Sen. Smith. “That’s why it’s critical to keep this economic engine on track by upgrading railroad lines and equipment, giving Minnesotans greater and safer access to national and international markets. Sen. Klobuchar and I are ‘all aboard’ on keeping Minnesota’s railway network reliable and efficient.”

“Twin Cities & Western is proud to partner with our Minnesota grain customers, the Federal Railroad Administration and our champions in Congress,” said Twin Cities & Western Railroad President Vic Meyers. “This project will ensure Minnesota farmers remain connected to the Mississippi River with safe, efficient and reliable rail service.”

The three grants are respectively awarded to the Twin Cities & Western Railroad Company, Minnesota Commercial Railway, and Northern Lines Railway. The grant funds come from the Consolidated Rail Infrastructure and Safety Improvements Program within the DOT, funded partially by the Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act both Senators worked to pass in 2021.

Twin Cities & Western Railroad Company will receive up to $22 million to buy 200 new rail grain cars and upgrade select tracks and rail infrastructure around Renville, Stewart and Hector in Greater MN. The new upgrades are needed to carry the new, larger and heavier grain cars that give farmers and producers the opportunities to sell more commodities at once. The Twin Cities & Western Railroad will contribute a 20 percent cost share to the project.

Minnesota Commercial Railway will receive $5.36 million to replace worn tracks in Minneapolis, St. Paul and Roseville. The project will reduce the risk of derailment and improve the safety and reliability of passenger and freight service in the Twin Cities metro. The Minnesota Commercial Railway will contribute a 20 percent cost share.

Northern Lines Railway will receive $1.3 million to redo approximately 25 miles of track in and around St. Cloud, Cold Spring and Rockville. The new tracks will improve safety for the railcars carrying freight and hazardous materials. The Northern Lines Railway will contribute a 35 percent cost share.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON MS NOW: “IT WAS AN INCREDIBLE VICTORY FOR THE AMERICAN PEOPLE AND A DECISIVE DEFEAT FOR MAGA EXTREMISM”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on MS NOW’s PoliticsNation, where he emphasized that after a historic midterm election victory, House Democrats remain committed to fighting for an affordable America and holding the crooks who are ripping off the American people accountable.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Joining me now to talk about it all is a man at the center of it all: House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries. Thanks for joining me tonight on PoliticsNation. I will say, Majority Leader—Minority Leader Jeffries, soon to be something else we’ll talk about. But first of all, I want to congratulate you on the Democrats’ strong performance. MS NOW estimates your party will hold 256 House seats, giving you a clear majority. What are your thoughts on how we arrived at this moment?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, good evening, Rev. Great to be with you. It was an incredible victory for the American people and a decisive defeat for MAGA extremism. Clearly, the American people are fed up. The cost of living is way too high. There are far too many people in this country—they’re working hard, they’re playing by the rules, but they can’t thrive and can barely survive. Democrats promise to fight for an affordable America. We promise to fight to lower the high cost of groceries and gas and housing and to fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American and, at the same time, in the face of all of the rampant, unprecedented corruption that has been unleashed on the American people, to hold the crooks accountable.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, any hope that these midterm results would prompt President Trump to change course and seek compromise seems to have already been dashed. His first major move after the midterms this week has been to elevate longtime aide Stephen Miller to White House Chief of Staff, replacing Susie Wiles. As you well know, Miller has been the architect of some of Trump’s most controversial policies, like mass deportations. And just earlier today, we learned that President Trump announced he has offered former UFC President Dana White the job of White House Press Secretary. It’s unclear if this is an official offer. What do these decisions tell you about where we are headed in the next two years?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Donald Trump and MAGA extremist Republicans are clearly tripling down on the chaos, the corruption and the cruelty. It’s a failed strategy, and the Republican Party, if they pursue this, will continue to crash and burn as we saw on Tuesday. Democrats are going to continue to focus on the issues that matter to the voters all across the country. We’re going to fight hard for people in urban America, in rural America, in small-town America, in the heartland of America and in Black and Brown communities all across America who want dramatic change in this country, and we’re going to work hard to deliver it.

REV. AL SHARPTON: Now, you announced in a letter to your colleagues on Wednesday that you intend to run for Speaker of the House in the new session. You have enjoyed unanimous support as Leader of the party during these past two terms in the minority. And so far, no one else has come forward to challenge you. However, Axios is reporting that more than a dozen lawmakers say Democratic House Members and Members-elect are being inundated with calls, and I put that in parenthesis, urging them to not vote for you. MS NOW has not matched this reporting. But what do you make of that? And what do you say to a voter who’s cast their ballot for Democrats seeking change, who might also be feeling some hesitance about having the remaining House leadership, even though even progressives voted for you to be the Minority Leader? Is this just noise? What do you think of this?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’re going to continue to work hard to make our case to every single current member of the House Democratic Caucus, as well as incoming member of the House Democratic Caucus. In the new Congress, we need to focus on affordability, accountability and bringing back to life American values like liberty and justice for all, equal protection under the law, access, in an unfettered way, to the right to vote and a return to our nation’s great heritage as a nation of immigrants. These are the things that I believe House Democrats have forcefully advocated for in the current Congress, against all odds, repeatedly pushed back against Donald Trump and MAGA extremists, battled them on every issue, battled them on the economy, battled them on tariffs, battled them on the reckless war of choice in Iran, battled them on ICE funding, battled them on the Epstein files and battled them on their corrupt and incompetent Cabinet officials and other members of the Trump Cartel, a few of whom we successfully ran out of town, like Kristi Noem and Pam Bondi. And so this was a historic victory for the American people, historic victory for House Democrats. We’re going to have an incredibly broad Caucus of great patriotic members. It’s been my honor to lead House Democrats over these tumultuous years. And hopefully I’ll have the opportunity to continue to work hard on behalf of the American people moving forward. We put it in the hands of the House Democratic Caucus members.

REV. AL SHARPTON: And you and I have talked a lot during the years, and I’ve told you the story. I was there in South Africa when ANC won the election in ’94, and Mandela said, ‘Now we have to govern.’ Now, everybody’s going to be looking for you and the Caucus to govern. What are we going to do? I’m certainly going to be pressing the John Lewis voting bill to come back and George Floyd bill. But I want to talk to you about Black representation. We mentioned at the top of the historic gains in terms of Black senators and Black governors. The situation in the House is more complicated. The Supreme Court decision in Louisiana and the gerrymandering wave that followed directly impacted House districts. So even in a blue wave, the number of Black representatives have gone down slightly from 61 Black Members to 58, not including non-voting delegates. That’s not as bad as it could have been or they intended it to be. But what can Democrats in Congress do to make sure it is not eroded any further?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we certainly are going to fight hard to make sure that we aggressively advance the John Robert Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act so we can end the era of voter suppression in the United States of America once and for all. We worked hard to make sure that we held some of the seats that were most aggressively challenged by Republicans in terms of unleashing this unprecedented gerrymandering scheme. We defeated the Republican scheme in Missouri that was trying to rip away a congressional district from Reverend Emanuel Cleaver. He’s coming back to the United States Congress. Don Davis successfully defeated a Republican gerrymander in North Carolina. He’s coming back. Shomari Figures also ran a great race. I campaigned with him on the final weekend in Alabama. They tried to gerrymander his seat out of existence and rip it away from African American voters in the heart of the belt that brought us the civil rights movement, and Shomari Figures is coming back. And we’ll build upon this progress to ensure that we have a Congress that continues to reflect the American people in every possible way.

REV. AL SHARPTON: And Shomari Figures will be on the show with me tomorrow. But we’ve talked a lot down through the years. You’re a member of National Action Network, so I know you always talk big picture. So let me finish by looking at the big picture for Democrats post-midterm. Since Tuesday, there’s been a lot of discussion about what the priorities should be. Should Democrats be prioritizing investigations of White House officials? Will impeachment be on the table or should the primary focus be on delivering in terms of affordability or all of the above? What is the focus—if you were to become Speaker—that you would be pushing for?

LEADER JEFFRIES: It definitively is going to have to be an all-of-the-above approach, but we have to relentlessly commit ourselves to making life more affordable for the American people in an environment where the cost of living is way too high. And no matter what part of America you live in right now, people are drowning in this failed Trump-Republican economy. And so, we’re going to work hard to move bills very early on to end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed gas prices on the American people. We’re going to work hard to reverse the Medicaid cuts, reverse the SNAP cuts. We’re going to work hard to end the Trump Tariffs, which have increased costs on everyday Americans by thousands of dollars per year. We also need to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits so we can provide economic relief to tens of millions of Americans who’ve seen their health insurance premiums skyrocket, in some cases, by over $1,000 per year. We’re going to work hard on affordability. We’re going to work hard on accountability, as we’ve indicated, because there’s a cost to corruption when you have folks who’ve been in office focused more on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors, as opposed to making life more affordable for the American people. And we’re going to work hard to bring about a restoration and return of American values.

REV. AL SHARPTON: So, you say all of the above. And I’ll have to leave it there. Thank you very much for joining us tonight, Congressman Hakeem Jeffries.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: SCHNEIDER CONDEMNS TARGETED CAMPAIGN OF ANTISEMITISM IN PHILADELPHIA

title: Heinrich, Whitehouse, Capito, Lee Release Substitute Amendment to Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026
text:
WASHINGTON – Today, U.S. Senators Martin Heinrich (D-N.M.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Energy and Natural Resources (ENR) Committee; Sheldon Whitehouse (D-R.I.), Ranking Member of the U.S. Senate Environment and Public Works (EPW) Committee; Shelley Moore Capito (R-W.Va.), Chairwoman of the EPW Committee; Mike Lee (R-Utah), Chairman of the ENR Committee; released a Substitute Amendment to the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act of 2026 (BAAJA). The Substitute Amendment includes clarifying, conforming, and technical edits to reflect feedback received since BAAJA’s introduction in September.

“I’ve worked hard to incorporate the feedback we’ve heard from Tribes and New Mexicans into this Substitute Amendment, and I’m proud to join my colleagues in releasing it today. The Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act will help lower energy costs, strengthen Tribal consultation, and create more good-paying jobs. It also makes sure data centers pay for the energy they use and the grid upgrades they cause, instead of passing those costs on to New Mexico families. Americans can’t afford to wait for lower electricity prices. We need to pass this bill now,” said Heinrich.

“I’m grateful for the input throughout this process from Senate and House colleagues, environmental and labor organizations, and Tribal leaders. Our manager’s amendment improves BAAJA and addresses the thoughtful feedback we have received. Now’s it’s time to pass this bill so we can lower costs, juice the clean energy economy, build big things again in America, reduce pollution, and create tons of new well-paying union jobs,” said Whitehouse.

“This substitute amendment preserves the foundation of the Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act, while making targeted changes based on feedback from our members and stakeholders to further build support. I’m thankful for my colleagues’ efforts to strengthen this legislation, the contributions from members of the House, and the support of countless organizations from across the country. I urge the swift passage of BAAJA to make life more affordable for American families,” said Capito.

“We have spent months working across party lines on both sides of Capitol Hill and with President Trump to deliver permitting reform that makes it easier to build in America. This substitute amendment reflects that work and brings us closer to getting the job done. Our permitting system takes too long, costs too much, and leaves too much uncertainty for the people trying to build what our country needs. We have an opportunity to lower costs for American families, and get America building again. It’s time to finish what we started,” said Lee.

title: LEADER JEFFRIES ON ABC: “WE ARE GOING TO VISIT ACCOUNTABILITY ON THE WRONGDOERS”
text:
Today, House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries appeared on ABC’s This Week, where he emphasized that with strong majorities in the House and the Senate, Democrats are committed to making life more affordable for the American people and holding the corrupt crooks accountable.

JONATHAN KARL: We begin with the man expected to become Speaker of the House in January, Hakeem Jeffries. Leader Jeffries, thank you for joining us.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Good morning. Great to be with you.

JONATHAN KARL: Obviously, a huge election for you. Have you spoken to President Trump yet?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I have not spoken to President Trump. It was a big night for the American people, a tremendous repudiation of MAGA extremism and a cry out for dramatic change in terms of the direction that we need to take to make life more affordable for the American people, to restore American values and, of course, to hold those who have visited unprecedented corruption on the American people accountable.

JONATHAN KARL: I mean, usually, at this point, I would have expected that the President would have reached out to the Democratic leaders. He hasn’t called you? Have you tried to call him, or will you try to call? I mean, you’re going to have to deal with him.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we’ll see what happens in terms of moving forward. But I have spoken to three former presidents, and I’m thankful for those conversations—of course, President Obama, President Biden and President Clinton, and many other leaders across the nation. And, most importantly, I’ve had the chance to speak to everyday Americans who were the ones that powered this election and want us to actually deliver a Congress that no longer functions like a reckless rubber stamp for Donald Trump’s extreme agenda, but functions like a separate and coequal branch of government designed to make life better for the American people.

JONATHAN KARL: It was interesting to see the President’s response to all of this. He didn’t cry fraud. He didn’t challenge the results, contest the results, not immediately anyway. And when I spoke to him shortly after Tuesday, he said to me, ‘I think we can get along. It’s good for the country if we do. The country has had enough.’ Obviously, he’s sent some different signals since then. But what’s your sense? Are you going to be able to work with him?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, the country clearly has had enough. And we’ve got to fight for an affordable America. The cost of living is way too high. There are far too many people in this country who are working hard, they’re playing by the rules, they can’t thrive and they can barely survive. People are drowning in this failed Republican economy. And enough is enough in that regard. That’s why we’re going to fight to lower the high cost of living on all the things. And we have to. We’ve got to fight to lower groceries and gas and housing, and certainly we’ve got to fight to make healthcare affordable for every single American. Now we’ll see whether our colleagues on the other side of the aisle actually are willing to listen to the American people so we can work to get things done. The good news is, Jonathan, that we’ve got a robust majority in a Democratic House and a robust majority in a Democratic Senate to be able to get to work.

JONATHAN KARL: So what is the goal? There’s kind of, there are two approaches you can take, oversimplifying a bit here. But you can pass legislation that you think the President might sign, or you can pass a whole series of bills that you know he’s going to veto. What’s the approach?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, the American people clearly want change that’s bold, change that’s transformational and change that is dramatic. They also want results because relief needs to come to the fact that so many people are struggling throughout this nation. And that’s everywhere. That’s in urban America, in rural America, in small-town America, in the heartland of America and in Black and Brown communities all throughout America. So from our standpoint, we want to do things like end this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has made life way too expensive. We need to stop the Trump Tariffs. We need to reverse the Medicaid cuts that put the health insurance of millions of Americans at risk and threatens to close hospitals all over the place. We certainly need to reverse the SNAP cuts. And we need to extend the Affordable Care Act tax credits. And hopefully, we’ll see some courage by a few of our colleagues on the other side of the aisle to work on these issues to get things done.

JONATHAN KARL: And the only way, ultimately, you get things done is if either he signs them or you get a lot of colleagues on the other side of the aisle to overturn his vetoes. There are a couple of things that I see where you could potentially get him to sign. I mean, President Trump asked Congress back in January to cap credit card interest rates at 10%. He also pushed for most-favored-nation status pricing on prescription drugs. And Republicans, Republicans never acted on either one of those. So will you—are those two areas where you could see passing bills in those two areas and saying, go ahead, Mr. President, sign it?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, we certainly need to provide credit card relief to the American people and we need to lower the high cost of healthcare across the board, and we look forward to working on those issues. There have been a lot of Democratic bills that have been put into the public domain, a lot of Democratic ideas to try to drive down health insurance costs and the cost of being able to just live and live an affordable life, a comfortable life and a good life. So we’ll see what the opportunities are. But we’re committed to moving aggressively during the first 100 days of the new Congress and beyond to keep our word, to fight for an affordable America, to bring about accountability because we’ve seen unprecedented corruption that has been visited upon the American people. And we are committed to holding the crooks accountable and making sure that Congress functions like a separate and coequal branch of government and a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch. And we also have to restore American values like liberty and justice for all, equal protection under the law, our commitment to the unfettered right to vote and to lift up our glorious history as a nation of immigrants.

JONATHAN KARL: You had some choice words for Stephen Miller’s elevation to Chief of Staff. You called him a ‘dangerous xenophobe and reckless extremist,’ said he ‘had blood—American blood on his hands.’ How does that—what does that mean for your ability to work with that White House, with that Chief of Staff, this President?

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s an awful choice. Stephen Miller is the architect of Donald Trump’s violent mass deportation machine and has unleashed billions of taxpayer dollars to brutalize and kill American citizens like Alex Pretti and Renee Nicole Good, and, at the same period of time, to violently target law-abiding immigrant families and communities all across the country. So you know, it was an irresponsible decision, in my view. There’s not going to be any opportunity, certainly, to work with Stephen Miller and what he represents. And we’re committed to forcefully pushing back against the extremism that they may try to continue to unleash on the American people. And we’ve got a firewall in the House and a firewall in the Senate, thanks to the American people.

JONATHAN KARL: Because, as I understand it, you talked on occasion or had some communication with Susie Wiles in your role as Democratic Leader, her role as Chief of Staff, which is natural in any White House, any Congress, but you’re saying that can’t happen with this new Chief of Staff?

LEADER JEFFRIES: It’s not going to happen with this new Chief of Staff to the extent that he lasts because he clearly represents, along with Pete Hegseth and a few others, a really toxic brand of political engagement, of politics and of governance. And the American people just voted for that kind of MAGA extremism to be eradicated, which is why they’ve been defeated up and down the ballot all across the country in the House, in the Senate, in governors’ races, in other statewide races and, certainly, in state legislative bodies.

JONATHAN KARL: Well, let me ask you about Pete Hegseth because Thomas Massie, of course a Republican, tells me that he intends to introduce a resolution of impeachment of Hegseth as Defense Secretary as soon as tomorrow. Are you going to support that? Will Democrats vote in favor of that impeachment resolution?

LEADER JEFFRIES: I’m a hard Yes on the Hegseth resolution. The so-called Secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe. Pete Hegseth has got to go.

JONATHAN KARL: And you’re confident all other Democrats are going to join you on that?

LEADER JEFFRIES: We’ll certainly have that conversation on Tuesday morning when we reconvene for the first time in Washington, D.C., but I believe there will be incredibly strong support for that resolution.

JONATHAN KARL: What about the rest of the accountability agenda? Your incoming House Oversight Committee Chairman, Robert Garcia, put it simply as to his agenda. He said, ‘Lawyer up.’ That’s the message to staffers in the White House, administration officials. Is that what it’s going to look like?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, there’s a cost to corruption. And throughout this campaign, we promised that we would focus, certainly, on affordability and driving down the high cost of living and on accountability in the face of the unprecedented corruption that we’ve seen unleashed on the American people by the Trump Cartel. As a matter of fact, our view has been, if you’ve got folks out there who’ve been shortchanging the American people, screwing over the American people or stealing from the American people, then they need to be held accountable in a manner consistent with Congress’s role constitutionally as a separate and coequal branch of government and a check and balance on an out-of-control executive branch. And my view is that we’ve got to follow the facts, apply the law, be guided by the Constitution at all times and then let the chips fall where they may on behalf of the American people and highlight the fact that there certainly is a cost to corruption when you have people in high office who are solely focused on enriching themselves, their family members, their friends and their donors, then they’re not focused on making life better for the American people. We’re committed to cleaning up the mess wherever it’s found. That’s in the Congress, in the Supreme Court and with respect to this administration. That’s why I strongly support banning Members of Congress from being able to trade stock as one of the things that we’ll need to do as soon as we’re back in control.

JONATHAN KARL: Do you expect Stephen Miller will be called to testify in some of these Oversight investigations—hearings?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, I’m going to defer to Jamie Raskin and the Democrats on the House Judiciary Committee, as well as Robert Garcia and Democrats on the Oversight Committee in terms of how they’re going to proceed. We’ll have a conversation about that over the next few weeks and I don’t want to get out ahead of any investigation other than making clear that we are going to visit accountability on the wrongdoers.

JONATHAN KARL: And we’re just about out of time, but I’ve got to ask you, what does it mean to you to be on the verge of being the first Black Speaker of the House in American history?

LEADER JEFFRIES: Well, listen, this is representative democracy, and it’s been an honor and a privilege to be able to serve the people of Brooklyn, as well as to work on behalf of the people of this great country. It was definitely meaningful as I closed this campaign with Shomari Figures in Montgomery, Alabama, the birthplace of the Civil Rights Movement, thinking about all of the struggles of those great heroes like Dr. King, Rosa Parks and so many other foot soldiers who helped to get us to this point. Listen, we have to continue to push back against the national nightmare that has been visited upon the American people. But I’m confident, standing on the shoulders of so many great heroes, that we are going to be able to continue this country’s long, necessary and majestic march toward a more perfect union.

JONATHAN KARL: Alright, Leader Hakeem Jeffries, thank you for joining us.

LEADER JEFFRIES: Thank you.

Full interview can be watched here.

title: WATCH: Pressley on MS NOW: “This Is Our Moment, And We Have A Mandate From The People To Match Their Energy”
text:
Pressley Calls on Democrats to Pursue Bold Agenda and Aggressive Oversight to Match the Mandate Voters Delivered on Election Night

“This decisive mandate from the American people [is] for the Democrats to not only demonstrate that we’re the adults in the room and know how to govern, but to prove that we are the fighters in the room.”

Video (YouTube)

WASHINGTON – In an interview today on MS NOW, Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley (MA-07), a member of the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, called on Democrats to meet the moment and use their new majority to govern boldly and aggressively pursue accountability for the corruption, cruelty, and economic harm inflicted by the Trump administration over the past two years.

Following Democrats’ decisive victories on Election Night, Rep. Pressley emphasized that voters delivered a resounding mandate not simply for Democrats to govern, but to fight for working families, expose corruption, and hold the Trump administration accountable for everything from its mass deportation agenda and deadly abuses in ICE custody to reckless tariffs, skyrocketing costs, and harmful DOGE cuts, which have disproportionately harmed Black workers and pushed Black women out of the workforce.

A transcript of the Congresswoman’s interview with MS NOW anchor Jacob Soboroff is below and the full video is available here.

Transcript: Pressley on MS NOW: “This Is Our Moment, And We Have A Mandate From The People To Match Their Energy”

MS NOW

November 8, 2026

JACOB SOBOROFF: Joining me now, Democratic Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley of Massachusetts. She is a member of the House Oversight Committee. Congresswoman, it’s great to see you.

REP. PRESSLEY: Good to be with you.

JACOB SOBOROFF: Thank you so much. What does what does going after the grift on day one look like to you, and who do you think should lawyer up?

REP. PRESSLEY: Well, first, let me just say I’m so grateful to this decisive mandate from the American people for the Democrats to not only demonstrate that we’re the adults in the room and know how to govern, but to prove that we are the fighters in the room.

That’s what the American people are looking for. That’s what they deserve, and that’s what this decisive midterm mandate is really demanding.

I’ve been on the Committee on Oversight since 2018 under the great Chair Elijah Cummings, may he rest in peace. Ranking Member Garcia, soon to be Chair Garcia, continues that that tradition of “the role of this committee is to be in the efficient and effective pursuit of the truth.” That’s what Elijah Cummings would always say.

And we know that sunlight is the best disinfectant, and we intend to bring it.

The unconstitutional, cruel, lawless, rogue actions of this administration across the board. Whether you’re talking about the racist, rogue, and dangerous actions of ICE, whether you’re talking about the fact that everything has become harder for everyone who calls this country home, except for people who call the White House home and are, you know, friends to Donald Trump as they’ve enriched themselves and their and their corruption.

You know, or whether you’re talking about the so-called actions of the Department of Government Efficiency, which took a sledgehammer to the infrastructure of our federal government and unlawfully pushed out many federal workers with a disparate burden on the Black worker, on black women in particular.

Whether you’re talking about the dismantling of Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Accessibility initiatives.

So we have the receipts, Jacob. The receipts are what the American people are experiencing every day.

This hostile fascist administration has been flooding the zone at every level of government and governing with contempt, and even weaponizing their agencies to go after their political enemies, most of whom are Black women who they’ve criminalized simply for doing their job. From Tish James to Lisa Cook to La Monica McIver to Ilhan Omar.

They have been flooding the zone, and this is our time. This is our moment, and we have a mandate from the people to match their energy.

So, although I am quite happy about the election results, I mean that’s really an understatement. I’m sort of in the mindset of Kobe Bryant. I don’t know if you’re a basketball fan, but remember in 200[9], Lakers versus Magic. Lakers were up two games, right? And they said, “Why aren’t you smiling?” And he said, “Because the job’s not finished. The job isn’t finished.

JACOB SOBOROFF: The job is not finished.” I remember, you know, I sat in that hearing room with you and Congresswoman Ocasio-Cortez and Congressman Raskin during the first Trump term as you conducted some of those oversight hearings, and I watched them myself as part of my reporting for this network, and the first Trump administration pushed back at almost every turn, tried to stonewall. Do you expect them to comply with these subpoenas? And if they don’t, what will oversight do?

REP. PRESSLEY: Yeah, thank you for talking about a lack of compliance because I’m not sure if I mentioned also their active obstruction of justice for the Epstein survivors they have stonewalled, obstructed, deflected at every turn. But we fully intend under the leadership of Chairman Garcia to use the full weight of our subpoena power.

And let me just say this, Jacob, we may not win every fight, but we have a responsibility to the electorate, to the communities and the people that we serve, at least to go after it. We may not win every fight, but we have to fight, and that’s exactly what I expect this committee to do. That’s what I expect all of our committees.

JACOB SOBOROFF: I want to show you a little bit of what the Attorney General said this morning on Fox. Todd Blanche, he was pushing back predictably against the Democrats’ comments about corruption in the White House. Let’s listen real quick.

TODD BLANCHE: I want to I want to be careful when we talk about government corruption. If there is government corruption, the people that are responsible will be prosecuted by this Department of Justice. But that’s different than a lot of the rhetoric that we’re hearing out there from Democrats about what they view, what they term as corruption, that actually is not corruption, but just an American success story.

JACOB SOBOROFF: It seems pretty preposterous, Congresswoman, to make this about the differences in the definition about corruption.

REP. PRESSLEY: Yeah, I don’t, you know, care what these folks have to say. If their lips are moving, they’re lying. They are completely disconnected from reality. They govern with contempt. They are clueless about the struggles of everyday working people. That’s why their president refers to affordability as a hoax. That’s why they trump up allegations of voter fraud. They were never afraid of voter fraud. They were afraid of black people voting. They were afraid of black women voting. And we did it to the tune of 94%.

So their president is the one that was trying to bribe voters in order to keep a majority. So they are desperate. We’ve got them on the ropes, we have the receipts to prove it. We’ll use the rule of law to continue to make that case and ultimately to hold them accountable. And the list is long. The list is long.

I have constituents who died in ICE custody simply for a toothache, an infection that went untreated, and their body went into sepsis and they died. So it’s not even just what happened to Emmanuel Damas or what happened to Alex Pretti or Renee Good.

It’s the black women pushed out of the workforce, which is a crisis for black women, families, and futures. And the black workers’ unemployment is at 7%.

Small business owners are struggling because of these reckless tariffs.

People are choosing between, you know, getting to work and groceries because of the cost of gas, because of this unauthorized war.

There’s a long sheet. There is a long sheet, but we are we are going to take them to task, and we are going to hold them accountable for what I consider really to be crimes against humanity: starving hungry children, denying people essential health care.

The list is long, but I have stopped wondering how low can they go, and have always been focused on how hard can we fight, and this is the moment to demonstrate that to the American people.

JACOB SOBOROFF: Thank you so much for being here, Democratic Congresswoman Ayanna Pressley from Massachusetts. It’s good to see you.

###
